recent_commits.message: Fix report()'s @return doc to match its actual invisible-attribute contract
recent_commits.body:
report()'s roxygen said it returns "the file path the report is saved
to", but it actually returns the module output invisibly, with the
save path attached as a save_path attribute (a vector, one per paper,
when called on a paperlist) -- the same pattern report_repository()'s
own, already-correct @return line describes. A caller following the
documented contract literally would get the whole module-output object
instead of a path (#451).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix R<4.5 paper() crash and crossref_doi()'s experimental Labs dependency
recent_commits.body:
paper() computed its random id with tools::md5sum(bytes = _), which
needs R >= 4.5.0, while DESCRIPTION allows R >= 4.3.0. read() builds
papers through paper() and swallows the error, so every read() failed
on R < 4.5 with only a misleading paperlist() message. Replaced with
digest::digest(serialize = FALSE), already a dependency and already
used the same way elsewhere in the package (#445).

crossref_doi() queried the experimental api.labs.crossref.org mirror,
which has no service guarantee, instead of the production
api.crossref.org/works/{doi} endpoint that crossref_query() already
uses and that returns the same fields. Also meant the existing
online("api.crossref.org") check did not catch a Labs-specific outage.
Moved the matching cached test fixtures from api.labs.crossref.org to
api.crossref.org accordingly (#446).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Fix OSF load-time hang and missing Hedges' g coherence check
recent_commits.body:
.osf_pat_validate()'s probe request had req_timeout(5) commented out,
so a slow (not down) OSF could hang library(metacheck) indefinitely
with no visible output (#449).

variants, so a reported Hedges' g was never checked for numeric
coherence against t and df, despite label_lhs() already classifying
it as an effect size for display (#450).

recent_commits.body: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): declare header_text_below_caption on every path and in the API reference
recent_commits.body:
5a6ab1f added the field to the PDF path and the Table TypedDict only. The full
suite at 17daccd failed 11 tests on it: the DOCX path did not carry it (the
additive-shape contract), the TypedDict pin did not list it, and the docs

recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): a trailing bare number moves onto the next heading only when the paper numbers its sections
recent_commits.body:
5a6ab1f moved any trailing single-level "N." past a section's appended
floats, which let the arabic folder glue it onto the next heading. A
125-paper census (2026-10-01, every case checked on the rendered page,
second model concurring) found four headings manufactured that way:
a running page number (10.5334/irsp.945 "43. Discussion", 10.5334/irsp.946
"31. References"), a sentence-final reference digit pulled out of its
sentence (10.1525/collabra.57785 "...in Table" / "8. Discussion") and a
notes item number (10.1177/19485506211056761 "4. Author Contributions").

Multi-level numbers still move on shape (every one in the census was
printed with its heading); components are 1-2 digits with a non-zero first,
so a bare cell value like 0.05 never qualifies. A single-level N moves only
when the document prints a numbered subsection of N or N-1 (10.1017/
jdm.2023.15 keeps "3. Results" now that Table 1 sits between "3." and
"Results"). Census after: the four wrong headings gone, no numbered heading
lost relative to v2.4.147, the multi-level and vouched single-level
restorations kept.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Pipe nested calls in tests
recent_commits.body:
* Chains start from a single object and end on the expectation, per the test style in AGENTS.md; no call nests more than two deep, and no pipeline runs inside a call that is itself a pipeline step.
* A chain fits on one line, or, if very long, breaks after every pipe. Consecutive parallel lines stay on one line with their pipes aligned; at the top level, a trailing `# fmt: skip` keeps air from undoing that.
* Replace the `_` placeholder, which needs R >= 4.3, with purrr::pluck(), mapply() with purrr::map2_lgl(), and evalq() with quote() |> eval().
* Keep the call forms that test-vectorize-test.R tests as they are, and leave Allard's reference code in test-grimmer.R verbatim.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pipe nested calls and pipeline verbs in package code
recent_commits.body:
* Calls nested more than two deep become `|>` chains that start from a single object, with a line break after each pipe.
* dplyr verbs and other pipeline functions are applied through the pipe.
* Tail return() calls are gone; return() is only used for early returns.
* Roxygen examples and vignette chunks follow the same rules.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop leading dots from internal variable names
recent_commits.body:
* Arguments of functions that also take `...` keep their dots, as they guard against clashes with it: those of function_map*(), seq_*_df(), and the functions the two proto factories return.
* The proto factories themselves lose the dotted copies of the formals of the functions they return, which read them from the enclosing environment instead.
* function_map() reserves the renamed locals that could shadow arguments of `.fun`.
* Drop a tail return() in function_map_total_n_proto() and a test helper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read the string `"NA"` as missing in `restore_zeros()`
recent_commits.body:
* It was reported as a value that is not a number, although it spells
  out a missing one and became `NA` either way.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject non-positive input in `grim_granularity()` and `grim_items()`
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_items(n = 0, gran = 0.05)` returned `Inf` without a word, and a
  negative `n` a negative count. Both now error via `check_positive()`,
  which lets missing values through.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep `unlist()` from coercing list elements in `is_numeric_like()`
recent_commits.body:
* A logical element next to a number became that number, and a factor
  its integer codes, so `list(TRUE, 1)` and `list(1, factor("a"))` were
  numeric-like. A logical value now makes a list `FALSE`, as it does a
  vector, and a factor is tested as its label.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give 0-row `audit_seq()` output the usual columns
recent_commits.body:
* `*_map_seq()` output records the dispersed variables as the `var`
  element of its `"scrutiny"` attribute. Without rows, `audit_seq()`
  can't read them off the `var` column, and it used to return only
  `hits_total` next to the reconstructed values.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Skip undecidable cases in `*_map_seq()` with `include_consistent`
recent_commits.body:
* A case with a missing key value has no verdict and nothing to disperse
  from. The default path dropped it along with the consistent cases, but
  `include_consistent = TRUE` kept it, and `seq_disperse()` then failed
  on the missing value.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep existing names of a matrix in `row_to_colnames()`
recent_commits.body:
* The name repair replaced every column name with a placeholder, not
  only the missing ones. A column whose header cells are all `NA` keeps
  its current name, so a named matrix lost that name to `V1`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Don't count unused factor levels in `duplicate_count()`
recent_commits.body:
* `table()` counts every level of a factor, so unused levels came out
  with a frequency of 0. Keeping only positive frequencies fixes that and
  also covers the ignored values, which the old filter removed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject an infinite `denominator`; unlist lists in `is_numeric_like()`
recent_commits.body:
* Both fraction functions share `check_denominator()`, which also rules
  out `Inf`, where `reround_to_fraction()` returned `NaN`.
* `is_numeric_like()` tests a list like the atomic vector of its
  elements, so a logical element is no longer read as a number.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove a zero-row branch misplaced into `audit_total_n()`
recent_commits.body:
* ea7e286 meant it for `audit_seq()` only. In `audit_total_n()`, it
  called `reverse_map_seq()` on total-n output, which fails.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Correct docs of helpers and mappers
recent_commits.body:
* The `absorb_key_args()` example no longer warns at top level.
* `manage_helper_col()` is called by `function_map()` mappers, not only
  by handwritten ones.
* The mappers take a tibble, and GRIMMER's verdict involves `sd`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare `duplicate_count_colpair()` values as strings
recent_commits.body:
* The other `duplicate_*()` functions compare strings, so the two
  disagreed on values like `0.1 + 0.2` and `0.3`.
* The docs now say that `total_x` and `total_y` exclude ignored values.
* `restore_zeros()` names the non-numbers it turns into `NA`, instead of
  leaking base R's coercion warning.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Align `grim_total()`, `items = NA`, and `reround()` zeros
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_total()` checks `digits_x` with `check_digits_whole()`, which
  now takes the argument's name for its message.
* `grim()` and `grimmer()` accept a logical `NA` for `items`.
* `reround()` adds zero to its result to drop a negative zero.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix small inaccuracies in `var`, `audit()`, and `grim_plot()`
recent_commits.body:
* `*_map_seq()` rejects a `var` outside the reported columns, and the
  docs no longer offer `items`.
* DEBIT's `audit()` counts distinct `n` without `NA`; GRIMMER's returns
  zero `fail_*` counts on output without rows.
* `grim_plot()` reads `reason` with `[[`, which doesn't warn.
* Docs of `grim_plot(n)` and `incons_to_prob` now match the code.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep the shape of mapper output at the edges
recent_commits.body:
* `*_map_seq()` without inconsistent cases returns a 0-row tibble with
  the usual columns, classes, and attribute, which `audit_seq()` and
  `reverse_map_seq()` now accept.
* A data column named like a result column is an error rather than
  being silently dropped.
* `recycle_digits()` attributes its error to the mapper, and
  `check_dispersion_linear()` names the function it was called from.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Convert unnamed matrices quietly in `row_to_colnames()`
recent_commits.body:
* `tibble::as_tibble()` without `.name_repair` warned about a tibble
  2.0.0 deprecation and told the user to report it to scrutiny.
* An out-of-range `row` is now an error rather than a silent no-op.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a non-finite `from` in `seq_disperse()`
recent_commits.body:
* A missing, infinite, or non-numeric `from` has no decimal level. It
  was blamed on `out_min` or failed deep inside `restore_zeros()`.
* The docs now say that the limits don't apply to `from` itself.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Handle empty and missing input in `duplicate_*()` and `grim_items()`
recent_commits.body:
* `duplicate_count()` builds its counts by hand, since
  `tibble::as_tibble()` fails on an empty table.
* `duplicate_detect()` and `duplicate_tally()` cut the flattened values
  into columns by a factor, which also works with no rows, and name an
  unnamed matrix's columns `col1`, `col2`, ...
* `grim_items()` ignores missing whole-number checks.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count decimal places of numbers under any `sep`
recent_commits.body:
* `as.character()` writes a number with a point, which was then searched
  for `sep`. Numeric input now always uses `"."`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix `function_map()` argument handling at the edges
recent_commits.body:
* A custom `.name_key_result` as `.col_names[1]` crashed every call:
  the column already had its final name, and the generated code renamed
  `consistency` anyway. The rename now only runs without `.col_names`,
  which must start with `.name_key_result`.
* `.args_defaults` naming a key or disabled argument, and `.fun` formals
  that the body's locals would shadow, are errors at creation time.
* `check_args_disabled()` reads the caller's dots with `...names()`
  instead of the call, which through `lapply()` names nothing.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read an `items` column in `*_map_total_n()`
recent_commits.body:
* The proto function rebuilt the data from the reported columns and `n`
  only, so an `items` column never reached the basic mapper. Helper
  columns are now carried along, one value per case, and un-merged
  afterwards like the `items` argument.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Stop `split_by_parens()` from overwriting existing columns
recent_commits.body:
* `dplyr::across()` wrote `{col}_{end1}` and `{col}_{end2}` over any
  column of that name, whose original values then replaced the split
  part. This is now an error, as is `end1 == end2`.

recent_commits.message: fix(render): a trailing bare number moves onto the next heading only when the paper numbers its sections
recent_commits.body:
5a6ab1f moved any trailing single-level "N." past a section's appended
floats, which let the arabic folder glue it onto the next heading. A
125-paper census (2026-10-01, every case checked on the rendered page,
second model concurring) found four headings manufactured that way:
a running page number (10.5334/irsp.945 "43. Discussion", 10.5334/irsp.946
"31. References"), a sentence-final reference digit pulled out of its
sentence (10.1525/collabra.57785 "...in Table" / "8. Discussion") and a
notes item number (10.1177/19485506211056761 "4. Author Contributions").

Multi-level numbers still move on shape (every one in the census was
printed with its heading); components are 1-2 digits with a non-zero first,
so a bare cell value like 0.05 never qualifies. A single-level N moves only
when the document prints a numbered subsection of N or N-1 (10.1017/
jdm.2023.15 keeps "3. Results" now that Table 1 sits between "3." and
"Results"). Census after: the four wrong headings gone, no numbered heading
lost relative to v2.4.147, the multi-level and vouched single-level
restorations kept.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables,render): keep the column labels a caption used to swallow; a float never splits a heading number from its title
recent_commits.body:
Two regressions the full suite found in this branch:

- Header labels deleted. flatten recovers blank column roles from statistic
  labels that leaked into the caption (10.1525/collabra.90203 Table 8
  '... Explicit Learning F p'). 3c8b475 stopped the leak, so when the grid had
  also missed its header row the printed labels reached no field. New Table
  field header_text_below_caption: exactly the span the caption no longer
  absorbs (old trim end vs new), reduced to its leading run of statistic labels
  in flatten's own vocabulary. flatten reads caption + this field, i.e. the
  same input it had before. collabra.90203: T8 'F p', T9 'df F p BF01 95% CI',
  every other table None.
- Heading split. The ligature fix in _locate_caption_anchor lets figures whose
  caption carries a ligature anchor in the body; on 10.1017/jdm.2022.2 Figure 2
  was appended after a section body ending in the next heading's orphan '5.4.',
  so '5.4. Discussion' was no longer rejoined. A trailing bare section number
  now moves after the section's appended floats (nothing removed).

Both tests (test_tables_flatten_blank_header_recovery, orphan multilevel)
fail without these changes and pass with them.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): review fixes -- flatten reads the DOCX declaration from the cells; caption walk robust to raised glyphs and wide spacing
recent_commits.body:
From a tier-2 cross-model review (Sonnet, 2026-09-28) of this branch:

- flatten._declared_header_rows read Table['header_rows'] as the author's
  ceiling. Since 4737846 that field is the POST-fold thead count, so a folded
  second header row went into the body: reproduced on 9 of 415 tables across 66
  real DOCX manuscripts. The declaration is now rebuilt from the cells' is_header
  flags exactly as docx_tables._header_row_count built it; DOCX flatten output
  is identical to v2.4.147 on all 415 tables.
- sync_header_rows: a table with no html and no cells now reports None, not the
  capture path's leftover 1; extract_tables_docx (public) syncs too.
- _column_lines: overlap judged against the smaller of glyph and line height,
  so a raised superscript that opens a line still admits its line's glyphs.
- _caption_text_from_column: lines above the caption are skipped by vertical
  centre (a raised glyph no longer drops the first caption line); the blank
  band is now > 1.2 line heights AND > 1.5x the caption's own smallest gap, so
  double-spaced captions are not cut after one line.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a blank gap right after a bare label does not end the caption
recent_commits.body:
The blank-band stop (previous commit) ended 10.15626/mp.2022.3108 p7 Table 3
after its label, printed alone on its line above a gap and the title. The
rebuild then returned nothing and the text channel interleaved the neighbouring
column: 'Table 3 Table 4 Study stimuli ...'. The stop now skips a gap that
follows label-only text. Found by re-running the caption census; the test fails
without the exemption.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a column-rebuilt caption ends at a blank band it measures itself
recent_commits.body:
The line grouping in 3c8b475 yields only lines with chars in the caption's own
column, so the old 'blank band' stop -- which fired only when the OTHER page
column printed a line inside the gap -- could no longer fire. On
10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901 p5 Table 2 the caption then ran on into its header
row ('... for datasets used Class Class Class Class'). A gap of more than 60%
of a line height between consecutive caption lines now ends the caption.

Found by the 125-paper caption census (v2.4.147 vs branch); the test fails
without this change and passes with it.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): header_rows states the header split the table's own html used
recent_commits.body:
Each capture path wrote its own guess: Camelot hardcoded 1, the layout path
'1 if any is_header else 0', the DOCX path 'n_header or 1'. The html's <thead>
(and flatten_table, which agrees with it) often used a different number: on
10.1525/collabra.90203 6 of 12 tables disagreed (Table 5: field 0, thead 3).
The field is now set from the html at both structured-extraction exits by
tables.render.sync_header_rows: <thead> row count, 0 when the html has no
header, None when there is no grid. Documented in docs/README.md and on the
Table type.

On the DOCX path flatten._declared_header_rows reads this field as the
author's ceiling; the synced value already had that ceiling applied, so
feeding it back gives the same split.

Owner decision 2026-09-28 (d-756293): make the field honest rather than
document the old guesses. Public field change -> consumer notice.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a table caption stops at its own header row; ligatures and symbol-font glyphs no longer break its anchor
recent_commits.body:
Three causes of one symptom -- caption text that is not the printed caption,
and the table it labels exiled to 'Tables (unlocated in body)':

- A lone statistic symbol on its own line (p, t, d, n, df, or a Greek-led
  symbol such as eta-p2) was read as a wrapped title word because it is
  lowercase, so the cell-run cut never fired. 10.1525/collabra.90203 p12
  Table 8 caption ended '... Explicit Learning F p'.
- The column caption rebuild grouped chars into lines by round(top); a
  symbol-font glyph sits a point or two off its line and became a line of its
  own. 10.1016/j.evolhumbehav.2016.06.001 p4 Table 1 came out as
  'Table 1 alpha Summary ... Cronbach's for ... HKSS. alpha' (the second alpha
  is the header row's). Lines are now grouped by vertical overlap, in one
  helper shared by the caption and column-body walks; a line-end hyphen is
  kept and the break dropped, the library's H1 convention.
- _locate_caption_anchor compared a caption still carrying U+FB01 against the
  normalized body; it now decomposes ligatures with the same function
  normalize used on the body (Hurst Tables 4 and 6).

Hurst: 3 of 6 tables were in the appendix, now 0. Two-sided: 12 new checks
fail on 05fb622 and pass here; 191 existing caption/anchor tests pass.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Test DEBIT's exact formula analytically and show its basis
recent_commits.body:
* `"exact"` now takes the range of `k` from `sum_range()` and checks the
SD bounds against `k * (n - k)` in whole-number arithmetic, folding `k`
onto the half where that product rises. This replaces a list of every
candidate `k`, so a row costs the same for any `n` (2e7 went from 1.3 s
to 0.01 s). The `"mean_n"` test moves into its own helper, unchanged.
* `debit_map()` returns `sum_lower` and `sum_upper`, the range of `k`,
which the old `x_lower` / `x_upper` columns could not explain.
* `debit_plot()` marks the attainable means `k / n` on the line, and the
vignette no longer says that a box crossing the line is enough.
* With more than 10,000 attainable means, `debit_plot()` draws only the
first mark in each cell of a 2000 x 2000 grid over the panel, found from
where the line crosses the grid lines, and says so. The plot looks the
same; `n = 2e7` went from ~14 million marks to ~10,000.
* `debit_plot()` errors if `data` has the DEBIT class but no recorded
`formula`. Class and attribute survive the same verbs, so such data were
built by hand, and guessing `"exact"` could draw marks that don't match
the verdicts.
* test-debit.R has an exhaustive oracle behind `run_full_debit_oracle`,
covering every rounding method with and without `symmetric`. It detects
exact ties itself, since `base::round()` misjudges them under `"even"`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make DEBIT exact for attainable means
recent_commits.body:
* The mean of `n` binary values is `k / n`, but DEBIT treated it as
continuous and accepted SDs no binary sample can have, e.g.
`debit(0.05, 0.21, 20, 2, 2)`. `formula` now takes `"exact"`, the new
default, which only tests means of that form, or `"mean_n"`, its former
only value, which keeps the previous test.
* `reconstruct_sd()` is gone: DEBIT was its only user and only ever
needed `sd_binary_mean_n()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn repeated reassignments into pipe chains with `call_on()`
recent_commits.body:
* A variable assigned two or three times in a row, each time from its
  previous value, is now one pipe chain. `call_on()` covers the steps
  that are a subset or a lambda, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x[!is.na(x)])`,
  which also stops a vector from having to be named twice to filter it.

* `head(-1L)` replaces the `x[-length(x)]` slice that started a chain in
  `write_doc_audit_total_n()`.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` and the manufactured function body in
  `function_map_seq()` are left as they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove remnants of string key values
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_plot(show_data = FALSE)` built its dummy data from `x = "0.00"`,
  so its default decimal count came from counting characters. It now
  uses `x = 0` and a `digits_x` column, like mapper output.
* `*_map_seq()` no longer guesses a missing `digits_*` column with
  `decimal_places()` on numeric values, which lose trailing zeros.
* `index_case_from_diff()` drops its branch for string sequences, which
  no mapper produces anymore.
* Drop `as.numeric()` calls and `x_orig` copies on key values that
  `check_newly_numeric()` has already required to be numeric.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a string `x` in `grim_total()` and `grim_probability()`
recent_commits.body:
* They coerced `x` with `as.numeric()`, so `grim_total("5.19", 20, 2)`
  returned a count where `grim()` rejects the same string. A missing `x`
  still gives `NA`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Start pipe chains in the tests with the object
recent_commits.body:
* Tests written since c3abc01 had fallen back to `f1(x) |> f2()` and
  nested `expect_*(f(x))` calls. They now follow that commit's model:
  `x |> f1() |> f2()`, with the expectation at the end of the chain and
  the pipes of parallel lines aligned.

* Only a compound first argument such as `list()`, `c()`, or
  `tibble::tibble()` still starts a chain as a call. `expect_snapshot()`
  code is unchanged.

* Extracting from a call's result is a step of the chain:
  `purrr::pluck()` for names and positions, `head()` for slices.

* Add the internal `call_on()` for steps that are an operator or an
  anonymous function, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x %% 1 == 0)`. It also covers
  `formals(f)$name`, since `purrr::pluck()` rejects pairlists.

* The suite passes with the same 19,570 expectations as before.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

recent_commits.message: Test DEBIT's exact formula analytically and show its basis
recent_commits.body:
* `"exact"` now takes the range of `k` from `sum_range()` and checks the
SD bounds against `k * (n - k)` in whole-number arithmetic, folding `k`
onto the half where that product rises. This replaces a list of every
candidate `k`, so a row costs the same for any `n` (2e7 went from 1.3 s
to 0.01 s). The `"mean_n"` test moves into its own helper, unchanged.
* `debit_map()` returns `sum_lower` and `sum_upper`, the range of `k`,
which the old `x_lower` / `x_upper` columns could not explain.
* `debit_plot()` marks the attainable means `k / n` on the line, and the
vignette no longer says that a box crossing the line is enough.
* With more than 10,000 attainable means, `debit_plot()` draws only the
first mark in each cell of a 2000 x 2000 grid over the panel, found from
where the line crosses the grid lines, and says so. The plot looks the
same; `n = 2e7` went from ~14 million marks to ~10,000.
* `debit_plot()` errors if `data` has the DEBIT class but no recorded
`formula`. Class and attribute survive the same verbs, so such data were
built by hand, and guessing `"exact"` could draw marks that don't match
the verdicts.
* test-debit.R has an exhaustive oracle behind `run_full_debit_oracle`,
covering every rounding method with and without `symmetric`. It detects
exact ties itself, since `base::round()` misjudges them under `"even"`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make DEBIT exact for attainable means
recent_commits.body:
* The mean of `n` binary values is `k / n`, but DEBIT treated it as
continuous and accepted SDs no binary sample can have, e.g.
`debit(0.05, 0.21, 20, 2, 2)`. `formula` now takes `"exact"`, the new
default, which only tests means of that form, or `"mean_n"`, its former
only value, which keeps the previous test.
* `reconstruct_sd()` is gone: DEBIT was its only user and only ever
needed `sd_binary_mean_n()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn repeated reassignments into pipe chains with `call_on()`
recent_commits.body:
* A variable assigned two or three times in a row, each time from its
  previous value, is now one pipe chain. `call_on()` covers the steps
  that are a subset or a lambda, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x[!is.na(x)])`,
  which also stops a vector from having to be named twice to filter it.

* `head(-1L)` replaces the `x[-length(x)]` slice that started a chain in
  `write_doc_audit_total_n()`.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` and the manufactured function body in
  `function_map_seq()` are left as they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove remnants of string key values
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_plot(show_data = FALSE)` built its dummy data from `x = "0.00"`,
  so its default decimal count came from counting characters. It now
  uses `x = 0` and a `digits_x` column, like mapper output.
* `*_map_seq()` no longer guesses a missing `digits_*` column with
  `decimal_places()` on numeric values, which lose trailing zeros.
* `index_case_from_diff()` drops its branch for string sequences, which
  no mapper produces anymore.
* Drop `as.numeric()` calls and `x_orig` copies on key values that
  `check_newly_numeric()` has already required to be numeric.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a string `x` in `grim_total()` and `grim_probability()`
recent_commits.body:
* They coerced `x` with `as.numeric()`, so `grim_total("5.19", 20, 2)`
  returned a count where `grim()` rejects the same string. A missing `x`
  still gives `NA`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Start pipe chains in the tests with the object
recent_commits.body:
* Tests written since c3abc01 had fallen back to `f1(x) |> f2()` and
  nested `expect_*(f(x))` calls. They now follow that commit's model:
  `x |> f1() |> f2()`, with the expectation at the end of the chain and
  the pipes of parallel lines aligned.

* Only a compound first argument such as `list()`, `c()`, or
  `tibble::tibble()` still starts a chain as a call. `expect_snapshot()`
  code is unchanged.

* Extracting from a call's result is a step of the chain:
  `purrr::pluck()` for names and positions, `head()` for slices.

* Add the internal `call_on()` for steps that are an operator or an
  anonymous function, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x %% 1 == 0)`. It also covers
  `formals(f)$name`, since `purrr::pluck()` rejects pairlists.

* The suite passes with the same 19,570 expectations as before.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix repo_check misses for 4TU, Dataverse, Figshare, DSpace7, and DataONE
recent_commits.body:
4TU (#431): .researchdata4tu_id() extracted a DOI-embedded uuid and passed
it straight to v2/articles/<id>, but the API needs a different numeric id
only a live DOI redirect reveals. Added .researchdata4tu_resolve_uuid() to
follow that redirect before querying.

Dataverse (#432): .dataverse_host_from_doi() returned the first host sharing
an ambiguous DOI prefix, picking the wrong DANS Data Station for a shared
prefix (10.17026, used by 4 separate installations). Now resolves via live
DOI redirect when a prefix maps to more than one host; also added the
missing phys-techsciences.datastations.nl prefix entry.

Figshare (#434): added collection-URL/DOI detection
(.figshare_collection_id()/.figshare_collection_articles()), mirroring the
existing project-expansion pattern. Share-links remain correctly flagged as
unsupported (no public API resolves them).

DSpace7/DataONE (#435): dataone_links() missed KNB's real #view/doi: URL
shape and had no fallback for a bare legacy KNB docid (knb.1404.1) cited
with no DOI at all. dspace7_links() had no DOI-based detection whatsoever,
so a paper citing only a DOI (never the host string) was invisible to it --
added live DOI resolution against known DSpace7 hosts.

#433 needed no change: 10.6078 was already added to
.dryad_doi_prefixes() by an earlier commit, before the issue was filed.

All fixes verified live against each issue's reported example. No
regressions in existing archive-dataone/dataverse/dryad/figshare tests.

recent_commits.message: Test DEBIT's exact formula analytically and show its basis
recent_commits.body:
* `"exact"` now takes the range of `k` from `sum_range()` and checks the
SD bounds against `k * (n - k)` in whole-number arithmetic, folding `k`
onto the half where that product rises. This replaces a list of every
candidate `k`, so a row costs the same for any `n` (2e7 went from 1.3 s
to 0.01 s). The `"mean_n"` test moves into its own helper, unchanged.
* `debit_map()` returns `sum_lower` and `sum_upper`, the range of `k`,
which the old `x_lower` / `x_upper` columns could not explain.
* `debit_plot()` marks the attainable means `k / n` on the line, and the
vignette no longer says that a box crossing the line is enough.
* With more than 10,000 attainable means, `debit_plot()` draws only the
first mark in each cell of a 2000 x 2000 grid over the panel, found from
where the line crosses the grid lines, and says so. The plot looks the
same; `n = 2e7` went from ~14 million marks to ~10,000.
* `debit_plot()` errors if `data` has the DEBIT class but no recorded
`formula`. Class and attribute survive the same verbs, so such data were
built by hand, and guessing `"exact"` could draw marks that don't match
the verdicts.
* test-debit.R has an exhaustive oracle behind `run_full_debit_oracle`,
covering every rounding method with and without `symmetric`. It detects
exact ties itself, since `base::round()` misjudges them under `"even"`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make DEBIT exact for attainable means
recent_commits.body:
* The mean of `n` binary values is `k / n`, but DEBIT treated it as
continuous and accepted SDs no binary sample can have, e.g.
`debit(0.05, 0.21, 20, 2, 2)`. `formula` now takes `"exact"`, the new
default, which only tests means of that form, or `"mean_n"`, its former
only value, which keeps the previous test.
* `reconstruct_sd()` is gone: DEBIT was its only user and only ever
needed `sd_binary_mean_n()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn repeated reassignments into pipe chains with `call_on()`
recent_commits.body:
* A variable assigned two or three times in a row, each time from its
  previous value, is now one pipe chain. `call_on()` covers the steps
  that are a subset or a lambda, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x[!is.na(x)])`,
  which also stops a vector from having to be named twice to filter it.

* `head(-1L)` replaces the `x[-length(x)]` slice that started a chain in
  `write_doc_audit_total_n()`.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` and the manufactured function body in
  `function_map_seq()` are left as they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove remnants of string key values
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_plot(show_data = FALSE)` built its dummy data from `x = "0.00"`,
  so its default decimal count came from counting characters. It now
  uses `x = 0` and a `digits_x` column, like mapper output.
* `*_map_seq()` no longer guesses a missing `digits_*` column with
  `decimal_places()` on numeric values, which lose trailing zeros.
* `index_case_from_diff()` drops its branch for string sequences, which
  no mapper produces anymore.

  `check_newly_numeric()` has already required to be numeric.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a string `x` in `grim_total()` and `grim_probability()`

  returned a count where `grim()` rejects the same string. A missing `x`

recent_commits.message: Start pipe chains in the tests with the object
recent_commits.body:
* Tests written since c3abc01 had fallen back to `f1(x) |> f2()` and
  nested `expect_*(f(x))` calls. They now follow that commit's model:
  `x |> f1() |> f2()`, with the expectation at the end of the chain and
  the pipes of parallel lines aligned.

(.figshare_collection_id()/.figshare_collection_articles()), mirroring the
existing project-expansion pattern. Share-links remain correctly flagged as
unsupported (no public API resolves them).

shape and had no fallback for a bare legacy KNB docid (knb.1404.1) cited
with no DOI at all. dspace7_links() had no DOI-based detection whatsoever,
so a paper citing only a DOI (never the host string) was invisible to it --
added live DOI resolution against known DSpace7 hosts.

#433 needed no change: 10.6078 was already added to
.dryad_doi_prefixes() by an earlier commit, before the issue was filed.

regressions in existing archive-dataone/dataverse/dryad/figshare tests.

recent_commits.message: Widen archive-member byte-range retry beyond the fixed 403/429/5xx list (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_bytes() -- the call .zip_member_fetch() makes for both a
member's local header and its compressed data -- only retried a response
matching .storage_is_transient()'s fixed list (403, 429, 500, 502, 503,
504). Any other status (a plain 401, a 400, or anything else not on that
list) was accepted as final after exactly one try, even when the identical
request succeeded moments later on manual reproduction: nothing
distinguishes "this host will never honour ranges" from "that one request
happened to fail" for an unlisted status.

.range_status_is_transient() now retries anything except 200 (host is
deliberately ignoring Range -- a fixed property of the host/URL a retry
cannot change) and 206 (success). Verified against a real, unmocked local
HTTP server that returns 401 once then 206 -- httr2's own retry loop
(req_perform1 -> retry_is_transient(), independent of req_error()'s is_error
override) correctly retries and succeeds on the second attempt.

httr2::local_mocked_responses()/with_mocked_responses() do not exercise
req_retry()'s actual retry loop at all (mock responses return through
handle_resp() before the while(tries < max_tries) loop is reached) -- a
limitation already independently documented elsewhere in this codebase
(test-repo-download.R's skipped "skip_on_api_limit = TRUE gives up on a
confirmed rate limit fast" test). Tests here check the request's configured
retry policy directly instead of trying to simulate multiple attempts
through a mock.

recent_commits.message: Widen archive-member byte-range retry beyond the fixed 403/429/5xx list (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_bytes() -- the call .zip_member_fetch() makes for both a
member's local header and its compressed data -- only retried a response
matching .storage_is_transient()'s fixed list (403, 429, 500, 502, 503,
504). Any other status (a plain 401, a 400, or anything else not on that
list) was accepted as final after exactly one try, even when the identical
request succeeded moments later on manual reproduction: nothing
distinguishes "this host will never honour ranges" from "that one request
happened to fail" for an unlisted status.

.range_status_is_transient() now retries anything except 200 (host is
deliberately ignoring Range -- a fixed property of the host/URL a retry
cannot change) and 206 (success). Verified against a real, unmocked local
HTTP server that returns 401 once then 206 -- httr2's own retry loop
(req_perform1 -> retry_is_transient(), independent of req_error()'s is_error
override) correctly retries and succeeds on the second attempt.

httr2::local_mocked_responses()/with_mocked_responses() do not exercise
req_retry()'s actual retry loop at all (mock responses return through
handle_resp() before the while(tries < max_tries) loop is reached) -- a
limitation already independently documented elsewhere in this codebase
(test-repo-download.R's skipped "skip_on_api_limit = TRUE gives up on a
confirmed rate limit fast" test). Tests here check the request's configured
retry policy directly instead of trying to simulate multiple attempts
through a mock.

recent_commits.message: Record call settings in one attribute, not in flag classes
recent_commits.body:
* Classes on scrutiny output are now for S3 dispatch only. Settings that
functions downstream need live in a single list attribute, "scrutiny",
read with the internal `scrutiny_meta()`.

* Basic mappers record every argument that applied to the whole call,
defaults resolved, as `args`. This replaces the "scrutiny_rounding_*"
and "scrutiny_percent_true" classes and makes `function_map()`'s
unreleased `.name_class_flags` argument unnecessary, so it is removed.

* Sequence mappers carry over the initial `fun()` call's record and add
`fun_args`, `name_key_result`, and `dispersion_linear`, replacing two
attributes and the "scrutiny_map_seq_disp_nonlinear" class. The
"scrutiny_seq_df" and "scrutiny_seq_test" classes became `seq_df` and
`seq_test` elements.

* This removes the regex parsing of class strings in `grim_plot()` and
`audit_seq()`, and the class rewrite in `function_map_seq()`. New tests
cover the recorded arguments, the sequence-test check, and the
rejection of non-linear dispersion.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Widen archive-member byte-range retry beyond the fixed 403/429/5xx list (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_bytes() -- the call .zip_member_fetch() makes for both a
member's local header and its compressed data -- only retried a response
matching .storage_is_transient()'s fixed list (403, 429, 500, 502, 503,
504). Any other status (a plain 401, a 400, or anything else not on that
list) was accepted as final after exactly one try, even when the identical
request succeeded moments later on manual reproduction: nothing
distinguishes "this host will never honour ranges" from "that one request
happened to fail" for an unlisted status.

.range_status_is_transient() now retries anything except 200 (host is
deliberately ignoring Range -- a fixed property of the host/URL a retry
cannot change) and 206 (success). Verified against a real, unmocked local
HTTP server that returns 401 once then 206 -- httr2's own retry loop
(req_perform1 -> retry_is_transient(), independent of req_error()'s is_error
override) correctly retries and succeeds on the second attempt.

httr2::local_mocked_responses()/with_mocked_responses() do not exercise
req_retry()'s actual retry loop at all (mock responses return through
handle_resp() before the while(tries < max_tries) loop is reached) -- a
limitation already independently documented elsewhere in this codebase
(test-repo-download.R's skipped "skip_on_api_limit = TRUE gives up on a
confirmed rate limit fast" test). Tests here check the request's configured
retry policy directly instead of trying to simulate multiple attempts
through a mock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Record archive-member download failures in download_repo_files() itself (#429)
recent_commits.body:
The previous commit fixed error propagation inside .zip_fetch_members()/
.zip_member_fetch(), but missed the actual call site the issue reported:
download_repo_files()'s archive-member block (R/repo-download.R) wraps
.zip_fetch_members() in tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL) and, on
any failure -- a thrown error, or a listing that returns NULL, or an
individual member coming back ok = FALSE -- just does `next`, leaving
file_location = NA with nothing recorded anywhere. This is the exact code
quoted in the issue.

Moved `failed`'s initialization earlier (it previously appeared after this
block ran, so there was nowhere to record into) and now populate it for
all three failure shapes, matching the has_url path's existing convention:
the roll-up message() and attr(files, "failed") already downstream pick
these up unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Record why a zip archive-member fetch failed instead of a silent NULL (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.zip_fetch_members()/.zip_member_fetch() collapsed every failure -- a
transient range-request error, a corrupt local header, a CRC mismatch, a
path-traversal rejection, a write failure -- into an indistinguishable
ok = FALSE with no message anywhere, so a corpus-scale run had no way to
tell a retryable failure apart from a host that will never support this.
Each failure path now records a one-line reason, and the five per-provider
download functions (Dryad, Zenodo, Figshare, Dataverse, ReShare) surface it
as a progress message and attach it as a `failed` attribute on the returned
table, matching the convention download_repo_files() already uses.

recent_commits.message: Persist zip_peek() to disk and thread skip_on_api_limit through it (#427)
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek()'s result was cached only in memory (.zip_peek_cache), reset every
R process, unlike repo_info_cache() which already persists a repository's
LISTING to disk for exactly this reason. Added an on-disk cache
(R/zip-peek-cache.R, mirroring repo-info-cache.R's shape: one file per
archive URL, opt-in via cache = TRUE) and wired it into zip_peek(),
zip_decision(), .zip_fetch_members(), and .code_expand_zip(), plus all of
their call sites in repo_check.R, data_check.R, code_check.R, and
repo-download.R.

Also fixed skip_on_api_limit not reaching zip_peek()'s own HTTP helpers:
.head_size(), .http_range_get(), .http_range_tail(), .http_range_suffix(),
.http_range_bytes(), and .range_size() all called .wait_out_known_rate_limit()
and the retry factories with no skip_on_api_limit argument, so a confirmed
exhausted rate limit was always waited out during a zip peek regardless of
what the caller asked for -- the argument only reached them via the global
metacheck.skip_on_api_limit option. repo_check() had no skip_on_api_limit
parameter at all; added one, and data_check()/code_check() now forward their
own skip_on_api_limit both to repo_check() (via module_run()) and to the
zip-peeking step, matching how they already forward cache the same way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Merge pull request #426 from scienceverse/fix-424-zip-peek-s3
recent_commits.body: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts, install-loop variables as packages, empty code files
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts (#424), install-loop variables as packages (#421), empty code files (#425)
recent_commits.body:
#424: zip_peek() on Dryad, Figshare and Harvard Dataverse
- These hosts redirect downloads to Amazon S3, which refuses HEAD (403)
  but honours ranged GETs. When HEAD gives no size, the tail is now
  requested by distance from the end ("bytes=-n") and the total read
  from Content-Range; a 416 answer is handled. The fallback reads the
  status before any body and accepts only 206, so a host that ignores
  the range cannot send a whole archive.
- A size is taken from HEAD only when the answer is 2xx; a 403 on a
  size request is no longer retried.
- .remote_size() falls back to a one-byte ranged GET the same way.
- Removed the OSF, Zenodo and Dataverse whole-archive routes in
  download_repo_files(): those archives never report a size, so the
  routes never ran. Removed .remote_content_length().
- Dryad, GitHub and GitLab archives now follow one rule: size estimated
  from listed file sizes, skipped when unknown or above 2x
  max_download_size, and stopped during download at 2x. GitHub and
  GitLab previously had no limit.
- osf_file_download(mode = "zip"): max_download_size is a budget for the
  whole project. A node whose archive does not fit is downloaded file by
  file within the budget (previously reported as "not downloaded" and
  then downloaded without limit). Partial archives are deleted.
- peek_zips now defaults to TRUE in data_check and reproducibility_check.

#421: dependency extraction
- code_library_names() no longer reports a variable's name as a package
  in install.packages(), requireNamespace(), or library()/require() with
  character.only = TRUE. Variables are resolved to the literal names
  assigned in the file (including for-loop variables, lapply(pkgs,
  library), p_load(char = pkgs)), and dropped otherwise.
- A package install.packages() cannot find is reported with its "not
  available" warning instead of "installed but not loadable".
- A 404 from the CRAN Archive is reported as "not found in the CRAN
  Archive", not as a network failure.

#425: empty code files
- code_abs_path(), code_setwd(), code_install_packages() and
  code_line_stats() handle an empty file without warnings or errors;
  code_parse_r() no longer reads the first line of an empty file.
  code_check previously recorded empty files as errored.

Tests
- New tests for all of the above.
- Existing tests: restore the real zip_peek() after tests that replace
  it; give new download tests their own repository names; add an
  renv.lock to the code_check green-light test (required since 9285b1f).

recent_commits.message: Persist zip_peek() to disk and thread skip_on_api_limit through it (#427)
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek()'s result was cached only in memory (.zip_peek_cache), reset every
R process, unlike repo_info_cache() which already persists a repository's
LISTING to disk for exactly this reason. Added an on-disk cache
(R/zip-peek-cache.R, mirroring repo-info-cache.R's shape: one file per
archive URL, opt-in via cache = TRUE) and wired it into zip_peek(),
zip_decision(), .zip_fetch_members(), and .code_expand_zip(), plus all of
their call sites in repo_check.R, data_check.R, code_check.R, and
repo-download.R.

Also fixed skip_on_api_limit not reaching zip_peek()'s own HTTP helpers:
.head_size(), .http_range_get(), .http_range_tail(), .http_range_suffix(),
.http_range_bytes(), and .range_size() all called .wait_out_known_rate_limit()
and the retry factories with no skip_on_api_limit argument, so a confirmed
exhausted rate limit was always waited out during a zip peek regardless of
what the caller asked for -- the argument only reached them via the global
metacheck.skip_on_api_limit option. repo_check() had no skip_on_api_limit
parameter at all; added one, and data_check()/code_check() now forward their
own skip_on_api_limit both to repo_check() (via module_run()) and to the
zip-peeking step, matching how they already forward cache the same way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts (#424), install-loop variables as packages (#421), empty code files (#425)
recent_commits.body:
#424: zip_peek() on Dryad, Figshare and Harvard Dataverse
- These hosts redirect downloads to Amazon S3, which refuses HEAD (403)
  but honours ranged GETs. When HEAD gives no size, the tail is now
  requested by distance from the end ("bytes=-n") and the total read
  from Content-Range; a 416 answer is handled. The fallback reads the
  status before any body and accepts only 206, so a host that ignores
  the range cannot send a whole archive.
- A size is taken from HEAD only when the answer is 2xx; a 403 on a
  size request is no longer retried.
- .remote_size() falls back to a one-byte ranged GET the same way.
- Removed the OSF, Zenodo and Dataverse whole-archive routes in
  download_repo_files(): those archives never report a size, so the
  routes never ran. Removed .remote_content_length().
- Dryad, GitHub and GitLab archives now follow one rule: size estimated
  from listed file sizes, skipped when unknown or above 2x
  max_download_size, and stopped during download at 2x. GitHub and
  GitLab previously had no limit.
- osf_file_download(mode = "zip"): max_download_size is a budget for the
  whole project. A node whose archive does not fit is downloaded file by
  file within the budget (previously reported as "not downloaded" and
  then downloaded without limit). Partial archives are deleted.
- peek_zips now defaults to TRUE in data_check and reproducibility_check.

#421: dependency extraction
- code_library_names() no longer reports a variable's name as a package
  in install.packages(), requireNamespace(), or library()/require() with
  character.only = TRUE. Variables are resolved to the literal names
  assigned in the file (including for-loop variables, lapply(pkgs,
  library), p_load(char = pkgs)), and dropped otherwise.
- A package install.packages() cannot find is reported with its "not
  available" warning instead of "installed but not loadable".
- A 404 from the CRAN Archive is reported as "not found in the CRAN
  Archive", not as a network failure.

#425: empty code files
- code_abs_path(), code_setwd(), code_install_packages() and
  code_line_stats() handle an empty file without warnings or errors;
  code_parse_r() no longer reads the first line of an empty file.
  code_check previously recorded empty files as errored.

Tests
- New tests for all of the above.
- Existing tests: restore the real zip_peek() after tests that replace
  it; give new download tests their own repository names; add an
  renv.lock to the code_check green-light test (required since 9285b1f).

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a text-free band between a ruled table and a caption is a figure, not table rows
recent_commits.body:
The narrowed note-distance rule (previous commit) rejects a distant "note" only
when running prose lies between it and the table. On 10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901

carries no text. So the caption came back as Table 6's note, the region ran
into it, and Table 6 reverted to fused label/value cells ("H:7,V:11 94.83").

disqualifies the gap too. Consecutive table rows sit 10-14pt apart, and a band

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): two region guards narrowed after a firing census and a cross-model review
recent_commits.body:
Measured every firing of the new detect.py guards over the 102-paper manifest
and judged each against the text it acted on. Two guards were wrong some of the
time. Both are now narrowed.

- The lone-rule filter dropped a table's OWN unique top rule:
  10.1038/s41598-023-50460-2 p4 Table 3 draws one full-width rule
  (x 159.4->552.2) above shorter recurring rules. 1 of 9 firings, confirmed on
  the rasterized page. Sol and Sonnet each raised the same shape independently
  in the consult round, and Sonnet reproduced it on constructed rules. Every
  correct firing dropped a rule BELOW the table (a footer separator, the next
  table's top rule), so only such a rule is now dropped. Final: 5 firings,
  5/5 correct.
- The note-distance rule assumed a ruled table's last detected rule is its
  last row. On 10.1503/cmaj.230841 p6 and 10.1177/00221465251343322 p7 the
  table continues far below the rules found, and the rejected "Note:" /
  "Source:" line was the table's real note. That was 2 of 32 firings; final
  output was unchanged in both, but the premise was false. A distant note is
  now rejected only when a running-prose line (spanning at least 60% of the
  column, no gap of 12pt or more, at least 25 glyphs) lies between the table
  and the note. Final: 21 firings, 21/21 correct (page footers, section
  headings, a figure caption, citation superscripts, a URL footnote).

The caption locator was 12/12 correct and is unchanged. Sonnet's
justified-stretch case (a word space of 6pt or more before a cross-reference)
is documented at the threshold as a known, bounded limit: it falls back to the
pre-v2.4.145 choice.

Each narrowing was mutation-tested: removing it turns exactly its new unit
test red.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): read Nature `N |` captions, and keep uncaptioned grids labelled instead of dropping them
recent_commits.body:
Two defects, found together on nature/nat_comms_1.pdf, owner-directed 2026-09-24
("investigate, understand what happened and fix ... best to retain information and
not drop. if unsure what that is - we keep but label it accordingly").

1. THE PIPE. The Nature family prints `Fig. 1 | Title` / `Table 1 | Title`. FOUR
   caption patterns required `.`/`:` (or a space and a capital) after the number,
   so every caption in that house style was invisible -- figures and tables alike.
   All four now build from ONE `CAPTION_PIPE_SEPARATOR` in tables/captions.py
   (captions.py x2, camelot_extract.py's caption-row and caption-number patterns);
   before, the second pair never learned the pipe, so the caption line stayed inside
   the grid as the table's first cell. A test asserts the four agree.
   Census, all 102 corpus papers: +29 caption matches in 5 papers, all Nature
   Communications, 29/29 real captions. End to end on nat_comms_1..5, same base,
   only the pattern differing: figures 0->5, 0->4, 0->6, 0->3, 0->5; tables +1
   (nat_comms_2), +4 (nat_comms_4), +1 (nat_comms_5), with real cells.

2. THE SILENT DROP. extract_structured discarded every Camelot grid on a page with
   no detected caption (and every grid no caption matched) with a bare `continue`:
   no event, no count, justified as "rare in the APA corpus" -- never measured.
   Such grids are now KEPT with the new field caption_status="uncaptioned_candidate"
   (label/caption None, id `u<n>`), counted as camelot_table_kept_without_caption,
   and rendered in their own "Uncaptioned table candidates (unverified)" section --
   never anchored inline, where an empty label would search for the bare word
   "Table". A grid overlapping a kept table on the same page (>= 50% of the smaller
   box) is a surviving copy and is deduplicated, recorded as such. Every Table now
   carries caption_status: matched / none_found (DOCX: the file declares the table)
   / uncaptioned_candidate.
   Corpus sweep: 83 of 102 papers gain >= 1 candidate, 369 in total, 40 deduped. A
   random sample is roughly half REAL statistical tables that were being thrown away
   (a regression table "Coeff. (SE)", "Odds ratio with 95%...", a 220-cell JAMA table)
   and half furniture (running headers, title blocks, figure internals) -- which is
   exactly why the label says "unverified", not "table".

THE FIXTURES WERE ON THE WRONG PAPERS. nature_minimal_rule ("minimal-rule tables,
gray-band header") pointed at nat_comms_1, which prints no table; nat_comms_figure_only
("figures, no tables") pointed at nat_comms_2, which prints a gray-band Table 1.
Verified by rasterizing both. Swapped, counts set from the printed pages (1 table /
4 figures; 0 / 5), and the sha256 text pins moved with their papers.

Gates that could only pass, now able to fail:
- smoke figure count: +/-6 tolerance accepted ZERO figures (two Nature fixtures
  extracted 0 while printing 4 and 5); zero is now its own assertion. The table count
  compares CAPTIONED tables, since candidates are extra by construction.
- four figure tests did pytest.skip("no figures detected") -- which is how zero
  figures stayed invisible. Now assertions. Two of them test figures/detect.find_figures,
  which has NO production caller and fails on this paper because pdfplumber collapsed
  every space in its layout text ("Fig.1|Lethaleffects..."): strict xfail, reason
  recorded, goes red the day that module works.
- test_wrapped_contact_strip: the contact block must stay out of the BODY (its name);
  it may now appear, labelled, in the candidates section. Scoped to the body.
- table ids may start `u`.

Two-sided: tests/test_nature_pipe_captions_real_pdf.py restores the old pattern and
requires the figures to vanish; the keep-and-label test was mutation-checked by
restoring the silent drop in-process -> "grids on this paper were dropped again".

CONSUMER-VISIBLE: every Table gains `caption_status`; Nature-family papers gain
figures and tables; 83/102 corpus papers gain uncaptioned candidates in `tables` and a
new appendix section in rendered Markdown. TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION left to the
release coordinator (one bump with the concurrent table-region fix).

NOT fixed, newly exposed, handed on: nat_comms_4 Table 4 is printed ROTATED and is
captured as caption-only with raw_text "Article" (the running header); JAMA's
unnumbered "Table." caption is another caption gap.

Targeted: 91 passed, 2 xfailed (then the caption-text assertion corrected: 5/5).
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a wider table region stops at its own table, not the page furniture
recent_commits.body:
2c8b0dd (v2.4.143) widened caption-anchored regions so wide tables stopped
losing columns. That is kept. But four detectors were never written for a wide
region, and a 102-paper diff (v2.4.142 vs 2.4.144) found real tables they
emptied or garbled. Every change is keyed on what the file states:

- `_bbox_of_caption_line` matched by CONTAINMENT, so a body sentence
  "presented in Table 4." above the real "TABLE 4" heading won
  (10.5465/amj.2016.1196 p19). A row whose match starts a text block (the first
  glyph, or after a gap of 6pt or more) is now preferred. With none, the old
  first-containing row is returned.
- `_widen_to_left_aligned_rows` buckets words by y across the WHOLE page, so a
  row "starting at the left edge" carried a side-note column
  (10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.48333 p6: the Model 1/Model 2 hazard ratios
  came out interleaved glyph by glyph) and a rotated copyright strip
  (10.1136/bmjopen-2022-066361 p6). It now runs only for a whitespace run (a
  ruled table's rules state its width) and skips non-upright words.
- the lattice union admitted a lone page-footer rule (x 47.9->562.8 beside
  eight table rules at 47.9->395.1). A rule that is the only one of its width,
  AND reaches beyond the recurring rules' extent, is dropped from the union.
- `_detect_footnote_below` took the first small text anywhere below a table:
  the rotated strip (bmjopen: Table 4 shipped with 0 rows), the page footer
  440pt below (10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901 Table 5, EMPTY), and a figure caption
  (its Table 6, EMPTY). Non-upright glyphs are excluded. For a ruled table,
  whose last rule is its last row, a note must start within one note-row gap
  (25pt) of it.

The note-distance rule was first applied to every signal. A geometry-only
census (all 429 captions, HEAD vs this) showed it moving 112 regions in 43
papers, and 10.1525/collabra.90203 Table 7 would have lost its lower 300pt.
Scoped to lattice, it moves 63 regions in 31 papers. A full
extract_pdf_structured diff over the 39 affected papers changes 15; each
changed table was checked against the printed page. No printed value is lost.
Recovered: jama_open_2 T2, bmj_open_1 T4 (now all 6 columns),
arxiv.2410.21901 T5/T6. Newly captured: 10.1016/j.jesp.2021.104154 T3.
Corrected: 10.1017/jdm.2023.15 T3 had carried Table 2's descriptives while the
regression table reached nothing.

NOT recovered: 10.5465/amj.2016.1196 Table 4, lost from v2.4.143 on. v2.4.142's
partial copy (M, SD only) existed only because of the mis-located caption. With
the caption now right, the table (rules drawn as rectangles, a lower-triangular
correlation matrix) is found by no detector. Reported, not hidden.

Two docstrings stated safety claims this disproved; corrected in place.
LESSONS L-060.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a ruled table no longer swallows the next table's caption and rows
recent_commits.body:
`_augment_lattice_with_stream_rows` (v2.4.94) appended every Camelot stream row
below a lattice table's box, to recover rows a ruling cut off. Stream does not
stop at a table: on a page of stacked tables it returns one block running
through the next caption and the next table. So a ruled Table 1 gained Table
2's caption line and Table 2's rows, mis-columned by stream ("Sleep vs
Nap-3.07"). Under Table 1's header (Effect | F | df1 | df2 | p) that row
flattened to `F(0.003, -0.31) = 98`, a statistic no page printed. docpluck
built it.

Reported by CitationGuard's and ESCImate's contract suites after v2.4.143 and
bisected to 2c8b0dd, which did not write the row. It made the region-driven
candidates correct, and `_pick_better_table`'s equal-columns tie-break ("more
cells wins") then chose the 8-row merged grid over Table 2's own 3-row grid.
Before that, Table 2's t-tests survived under Table 1's caption.

The run of appended rows now stops at the top edge of another same-page ruled
table sharing its x-range, or at a `Table N.` / `Figure N.` caption row. The box
is widened only to the last row actually appended. Each stop is recorded as
`lattice_augment_stopped_at_boundary`.

Measured over the 102-paper manifest: it fires 6 times in 5 papers
(5 caption_row, 1 sibling_table). 6/6 withheld only a caption line, body prose
or another table's rows, and 0 withheld a row of the table it was attached to.
One final table changes: 10.1038/s41598-023-50401-z Table 1 loses its own
caption and three rows of Discussion prose ("no significant difference
(P = 0.16) ..."), confirmed on the rasterized p4.

Tests: a reportlab-built stacked-tables page fails on 14ba3b8, 2c8b0dd and
2c8b0dd^ and passes here. Four augmenter unit tests. Each of the three
conditions was mutation-tested; removing any one turns at least one test red.

(eta before `2 =`) and S5b (>= / <= before a number) still rewrite U+FFFD from context.

returns all 9; after normalize_text, S5b has rewritten all 9 and 0 remain.

recent_commits.message: fix(extract): retire the U+FFFD recovery -- it could substitute a wrong statistic
recent_commits.body:
Owner decision 2026-09-24. When pdftotext emitted three or more U+FFFD, extract_pdf
ran pdfplumber over the whole document and then either REPLACED the entire text
(Mode A) or patched words one at a time from a global token set (Mode B). Every
load-bearing claim against it was reproduced by running the code:

  * Mode A's guard, _reading_order_agrees, returned True for a document's exact
    REVERSE (under 2000 chars it checks length only), for its blocks SHUFFLED
    (it tests substring membership, never order), and for completely UNRELATED
    text (when no clean 60-char window exists it skips all three checks and
    returns True vacuously).
  * Mode A joined pages with "\n\n" instead of form feeds, so every downstream
    page boundary collapsed to page 1.
  * Mode B turned `partial <U+FFFD>2 = .35` into `partial R2 = .35` -- a partial
    eta-squared relabelled as an R-squared -- because "unique" meant unique among
    distinct token spellings anywhere in the document, and the SMP Greek it
    looked up had already been spelled out, so the true `eta2` could never match.
  * Mode B is not dormant: on vancouver/plos_med_1.pdf (9 U+FFFD) it EXECUTED on
    the live document and returned 0 patches only because no word had a unique
    look-alike.
  * Across all 102 corpus papers neither mode was ever accepted.

A visible U+FFFD is a flag a consumer can act on; a plausible wrong token is not.
Removed: the recovery block and every helper that served only it
(_patch_fffds_word_by_word, _reading_order_agrees, _build_smp_greek /
_SMP_GREEK_TO_ASCII, _smp_to_ascii_map, _recover_with_pdfplumber). Nothing
correctly encoded is lost: normalize.py maps SMP math-italic characters that
pdftotext DOES decode (_MATH_ALNUM_RE), and the removed Greek table was the
second copy that the ONE-CONCEPT-ONE-TABLE rule was written about.

Tests: the eight word-patch unit tests and test_smp_greek_agrees_with_a5.py (all
five of its tests exercised only the removed table) are gone. The strict xfail
test_nature_smp_recovery, whose premise had been false since 2026-09-17, is
replaced by test_replacement_characters_pass_through_as_printed on the one corpus
paper that carries U+FFFD. Mutation-checked: making extract_pdf rewrite U+FFFD
turns it red ("found 0"). The compat allowlist no longer accepts a method value
that cannot be produced. Docs, README, SYMBOL_CONTRACT and DESIGN updated; the
DESIGN section is kept and marked retired.

CONSUMER-VISIBLE:
  method   before: "pdftotext_default+pdfplumber_recovery" / "...+pdfplumber_word_patch"
           after:  never produced
  text     before: on >= 3 U+FFFD, possibly a different document's worth of text
           after:  U+FFFD passed through as printed
  fallbacks: "pdfplumber_recovery_exception" no longer emitted
No corpus paper's output changes; the change bites only outside the corpus.

python -m pytest tests/test_extraction.py tests/test_v23_1_fixes.py
  tests/test_v2_backwards_compat.py tests/test_mathitalic_greek_real_pdf.py
  tests/test_symbol_contract.py tests/test_public_repo_hygiene.py -n 4
  -> 162 passed

recent_commits.message: Fix `debit_plot()` and plot argument handling
recent_commits.body:
* `debit_plot()` recycled the `n` column along a single DEBIT line; it
  now draws the line for the correct `n`. If `n` varies, it draws the
  lines for the smallest and largest `n` and shades the band between
  them, which contains all the others. `NA` rows are dropped with a
  warning, and it returns its plot rather than printing it.
* `debit_plot()` no longer draws outer boxes around the rectangles;
  `show_outer_boxes` and the `tile_*` arguments are gone. Each rectangle
  is drawn over a point at the reported mean and SD instead, so that it
  shows up even when it is too small to see.
* `grim_plot(n = ...)` now ends the x-axis at `n`, and
  `split_by_digits = TRUE` always returns a list.
* `grim_plot_values()` and `grimmer_plot_values()` reject invalid input
  with clear errors.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix duplicate counts and audit summary statistics
recent_commits.body:
* `audit()` of `duplicate_detect()` output dropped columns without
  duplicates, which also skewed `.total`.
* `duplicate_count_colpair()`'s `rate_y` could exceed 1.
* `audit_summary_stats()` computed `na_rate` for `.total` over rows, not
  values, and gave `Inf`/`-Inf` for all-`NA` columns.
* `duplicate_count()` now uses a named vector's names as `locations`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Split parenthesized strings one at a time
recent_commits.body:
* The split pieces were pooled and re-chunked by their average count, so
one cell with an extra pair of parentheses shifted every later value
into the wrong row. Separators are now matched literally, `NA` no
longer breaks `split_by_parens()`, and `transform = TRUE` no longer
mixes up columns such as `exp_sd`. `row_to_colnames()` handles `NA`
header cells.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix decimal counting, `restore_zeros()`, and rounding input checks
recent_commits.body:
* `sep` is matched literally, as documented; the default is now `"."`.
* `decimal_places()` and `decimal_places_scalar()` agree on malformed
  strings and read `"inf"`/`"nan"` in any case.
* `restore_zeros()` handled scientific notation and wide padding badly.
* `reround()` and `unround()` validate `digits` alike; `unround()`
  treats an infinite `x` as missing.
* `rounding_bias()`, the `round_*()` functions, and
  `reround_to_fraction()` handle strings, `symmetric`, recycling, and
  `NA` properly.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix sequence, dispersion, and total-n edge cases
recent_commits.body:
* `reverse_map_total_n()` rebuilt the wrong total `n` unless
  `dispersion` started at 0.
* `seq_endpoint()` and `seq_distance()` drifted off the decimal level.
* `is_seq_linear()` accepted zigzags; the other predicates returned `NA`
  where the known values ruled a sequence out.
* `seq_disperse()` accepted a fractional `dispersion` and compared
  string limits as strings.
* `disperse_total()` and the total-n mappers crashed when no pair of
  group sizes was left, for a total below 2, and for 0-row data.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make the GRIM probability exact for every rounding method
recent_commits.body:
* `(10^D - N * L) / 10^D` only holds for rounding methods with a single
half-open range one step wide. `"up_or_down"` admits ties toward both
neighbors, and `"ceiling_or_floor"` a range two steps wide.
`grim_probability()` and `grim_total()` now take `rounding` and
`threshold` and count exactly the values `grim()` rules out, and return
`NA` where `grim()` does. `grim_map()` passes its `rounding` on.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Close gaps in the tests' handling of untestable input
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer()` checked the scale bounds before `n`, turning undecidable
  cases into `FALSE`. A negative `sd` is now `FALSE` with its own reason.
* `grim_values()` and `grim_closest()` skipped the decidability check.
* `grim_binomial()` and `grim_binomial_power()` crashed R on empty
  input inside poibin.
* A string `n` and an infinite `digits_*` now get clear errors.
* The missing-`digits_sd` error suggested a call that itself failed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Anchor the patterns of `is_map_df()` and friends
recent_commits.body:
* `(^scrutiny_)*` made the prefix optional, so any class ending in `_map`
matched, and `is_map_basic_df()` rejected mappers with `map` in their
test name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read key arguments by value in `absorb_key_args()`
recent_commits.body:
* It parsed the unevaluated call, which through `lapply()` or
`purrr::map()` is `FUN(X[[i]], ...)`, and from a wrapper names a
variable rather than the column. It also silently ignored a key argument
whenever `data` already had a column of that name. The values are now
captured in the mapper's frame, and such a clash is an error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix `items` and `case` in `*_map_seq()` output
recent_commits.body:
* The sequence mappers re-tested `n * items` with `items = 1`. GRIMMER
  needs `n` and `items` separately, so `grimmer_map_seq()` gave wrong
  verdicts, even for the reported values. `function_map()` now records
  which key column each helper is merged into, and `function_map_seq()`
  undoes the merge: `n` is dispersed as the sample size and `items` is
  returned as a column, which `audit_seq()` also reads.
* `case` is now the row number in the input data, not the position
  among the inconsistent rows, so results can be joined back.
* `audit_seq()` now accepts output from a single-step `dispersion`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

around on main. Now using the documented pattern for custom expectations
instead: https://testthat.r-lib.org/articles/custom-expectation.html

recent_commits.message: Persist zip_peek() to disk and thread skip_on_api_limit through it (#427)
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek()'s result was cached only in memory (.zip_peek_cache), reset every
R process, unlike repo_info_cache() which already persists a repository's
LISTING to disk for exactly this reason. Added an on-disk cache
(R/zip-peek-cache.R, mirroring repo-info-cache.R's shape: one file per
archive URL, opt-in via cache = TRUE) and wired it into zip_peek(),
zip_decision(), .zip_fetch_members(), and .code_expand_zip(), plus all of
their call sites in repo_check.R, data_check.R, code_check.R, and
repo-download.R.

Also fixed skip_on_api_limit not reaching zip_peek()'s own HTTP helpers:
.head_size(), .http_range_get(), .http_range_tail(), .http_range_suffix(),
.http_range_bytes(), and .range_size() all called .wait_out_known_rate_limit()
and the retry factories with no skip_on_api_limit argument, so a confirmed
exhausted rate limit was always waited out during a zip peek regardless of
what the caller asked for -- the argument only reached them via the global
metacheck.skip_on_api_limit option. repo_check() had no skip_on_api_limit
parameter at all; added one, and data_check()/code_check() now forward their
own skip_on_api_limit both to repo_check() (via module_run()) and to the
zip-peeking step, matching how they already forward cache the same way.
