recent_commits.body: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts, install-loop variables as packages, empty code files
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts (#424), install-loop variables as packages (#421), empty code files (#425)
recent_commits.body:
#424: zip_peek() on Dryad, Figshare and Harvard Dataverse
- These hosts redirect downloads to Amazon S3, which refuses HEAD (403)
  but honours ranged GETs. When HEAD gives no size, the tail is now
  requested by distance from the end ("bytes=-n") and the total read
  from Content-Range; a 416 answer is handled. The fallback reads the
  status before any body and accepts only 206, so a host that ignores
  the range cannot send a whole archive.
- A size is taken from HEAD only when the answer is 2xx; a 403 on a
  size request is no longer retried.
- .remote_size() falls back to a one-byte ranged GET the same way.
- Removed the OSF, Zenodo and Dataverse whole-archive routes in
  download_repo_files(): those archives never report a size, so the
  routes never ran. Removed .remote_content_length().
- Dryad, GitHub and GitLab archives now follow one rule: size estimated
  from listed file sizes, skipped when unknown or above 2x
  max_download_size, and stopped during download at 2x. GitHub and
  GitLab previously had no limit.
- osf_file_download(mode = "zip"): max_download_size is a budget for the
  whole project. A node whose archive does not fit is downloaded file by
  file within the budget (previously reported as "not downloaded" and
  then downloaded without limit). Partial archives are deleted.
- peek_zips now defaults to TRUE in data_check and reproducibility_check.

#421: dependency extraction
- code_library_names() no longer reports a variable's name as a package
  in install.packages(), requireNamespace(), or library()/require() with
  character.only = TRUE. Variables are resolved to the literal names
  assigned in the file (including for-loop variables, lapply(pkgs,
  library), p_load(char = pkgs)), and dropped otherwise.
- A package install.packages() cannot find is reported with its "not
  available" warning instead of "installed but not loadable".
- A 404 from the CRAN Archive is reported as "not found in the CRAN
  Archive", not as a network failure.

#425: empty code files
- code_abs_path(), code_setwd(), code_install_packages() and
  code_line_stats() handle an empty file without warnings or errors;
  code_parse_r() no longer reads the first line of an empty file.
  code_check previously recorded empty files as errored.

Tests
- New tests for all of the above.
- Existing tests: restore the real zip_peek() after tests that replace
  it; give new download tests their own repository names; add an
  renv.lock to the code_check green-light test (required since 9285b1f).

recent_commits.message: Convert Grobid TEI to bibr export schema 12.0
recent_commits.body:
grobid_to_bibr(schema_version = "12.0") converts Grobid TEI into a 12.x
paper and saves it as a 12.0 file:

- ids are 1-based positions in document order;
- xref targets come from the xml:id each <ref> points at, for bib,
  figure, table and foot references;
- each caption and footnote is one text row with no section, after the
  body and the reference list, and there are no pseudo-sections; a
  caption starts with its printed label, taken from <head> when figDesc
  leaves it out;
- the source is the PDF next to the TEI (published.pdf for
  published.pdf.tei.xml), else the TEI, so source.sha256 matches a bibr
  export of the same PDF; paper_id is the source's name without its
  extension;
- the producer is Grobid, with the version in the TEI header, and the
  converter is metacheck; completed_at is when Grobid extracted the
  content, from the same header, else the time of the conversion;
- metacheck's own warning codes start with METACHECK_.

The body sentences are made as before. Without schema_version, the
conversion is unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Write bibr export schema 12.0 with paper_write()
recent_commits.body:
paper_write(schema_version = "12.0") saves a paper read from a bibr 12.0
export as a 12.0 file. It keeps the paper's extraction block, so a bibr
export keeps bibr as its producer and bibr's completed_at, and names
metacheck as the converter: rewriting bibr's exports changes nothing but
converter. bib_match rows made by add_bib_match() are converted to the
12.0 columns, and a score that is not on the 0-1 scale is written as null
with a METACHECK_MATCH_SCORE_NOT_0_1 warning. A paper in the older format
is refused, and so is one read from a later 12.x, since its rewrite would
have to keep keys metacheck does not know. Without schema_version,
paper_write() writes what it wrote before.

The tests validate what they write against bibr's strict schema (a copy
in tests/testthat/fixtures/bibr12) when jsonvalidate, now in Suggests, is
installed.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Read bibr export schema 12.x files
recent_commits.body:
.read_bibr() now sends a file with a root schema_version (bibr export
schema 11 and later) to .read_bibr12(), which reads 12.x and stops on any
other version. Files without a root schema_version read exactly as
before. Keys that a later 12.x adds are ignored.

A 12.x paper keeps metacheck's info table, made from metadata and source,
and info_match (metadata_match); the other tables keep their 12.x names
and meanings. Captions and footnotes are text rows with no section that
figure, table and the new footnote table point at with text_id; xref_id
is the row's own key and target_id the row it cites; paper$extraction
holds the export's extraction block. Degrees of freedom stay in
parentheses, as metacheck's statistics code expects.

inst/schema/paper-bibr12.json lists the optional tables and columns this
adds. paper_validate() and .paper_coerce() merge it into paper.json and
skip properties that are not tables (extraction); paper() and paper.json
are unchanged. ref_consistency, ref_miscitation and the table captions of
match_reported_output() read 12.x papers, and ref_accuracy compares the
0-1 match scores of 12.x papers with suggest_score / 100.

recent_commits.body:

overlap), so checks.py refused it and it gated nothing -- and its keys were the
old filename slugs, 25 of them titles of unsubmitted manuscripts. Rebuilt from a
whole-corpus run of library HEAD + the app service that ships with it (405
doc x level cells, 1620 check results: pass 1492, fail 26, skip 102).

app (origin/master): 0 pass->fail, 6 fail->pass. Section output identical on
403/403 cells. The 17 table-content differences are load nondeterminism: within
EACH arm 7-8 papers' tables differ across normalization levels (tables do not
depend on level), and sci-rep-2 re-run standalone on v2.4.143 3x reproduces the
new arm's tables. All 135 keys join the manifest; non-corpus keys are all
<source>__<16 hex>.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): one DOI grammar, not two — and the count that says the fix is inert
recent_commits.body:
`_DOI_IDENTIFIER_IN_LINE` (H0's colon-lead-in exemption) and
`_BARE_DOI_IDENTIFIER_LINE` (P0r's running-footer predicate) each hand-typed the
DOI grammar, nine lines apart in the same commit, under a comment on the first
one warning that a second copy WILL drift. It had already drifted: printing both
regexes' verdict on `doi:10/gt3vmw` gave False and True. Both now derive from a
shared `_DOI_FULL_FORM` / `_DOI_SHORT_FORM` pair. Found by /docpluck-review.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.67 -> 1.9.68, because the unification WIDENS one
predicate: a `doi:`-prefixed short-form DOI on a colon-introduced header-zone
line now survives where it did not. That is a consumer-visible text change for
that shape, and an unbumped version would make pre-fix and post-fix output
indistinguishable in a consumer's own store.

PREVALENCE, MEASURED — because the divergence was found by a CONSTRUCTED string,
which is evidence about the code and never about the corpus. Over 200 PDFs (199
English; 1 Spanish excluded and reported) sampled seed 20260912: the newly-exempt
shape occurs 0 lines in 0 papers. Two-sided, so that zero is a property of the
corpus and not of a broken search — the same scan's control, any bare short-form
`10/xxxx`, fires on 8 lines in 8 papers. Confirmed a second way: the canary
paper's render is byte-identical across the change (sha256 8d74f263ec2b0f03...).
So this is kept because it removes a duplicated grammar, NOT because a paper was
losing a DOI to it, and it must not later be cited as a corpus defect.

Ships tools/diag/doi_short_form_prevalence.py, which regenerates those numbers.
The comment named the tool, so the tool exists; and every site quoting the counts
names the command, so none of them is a number nobody can reproduce.

Also in this commit, both found while verifying the above:

- CHANGELOG.md had TWO `## [2.4.143]` headings after the review's edit. One
  version, one entry: merged, with the 1.9.67 work now a section under it.

- tests/test_cli_structured.py spawns real `python -m docpluck` subprocesses on a
  fixed 120s budget. Under `pytest -n auto` on 14 workers that expires:
  test_figures_only_omits_tables and test_html_tables_to_writes_html_files
  reported FAILED on subprocess.TimeoutExpired while the same file passed 7/7
  serially in 192s. A false RED in the release gate costs more than a false green
  — it sends someone hunting a regression that does not exist. The budget now
  scales with load, as tests/test_benchmark_docx_html.py already does; both
  branches were proved to fire (480 under a worker, 120 serial). It is a timeout,
  not an assertion, so a genuinely hung CLI still fails.

LESSONS.md L-057: a comment predicting drift is evidence someone thought about
the risk, never evidence it was checked for. Its second half records the
prevalence, so a later reader cannot mistake L-057 for a corpus defect.

  body and the reference list, and there are no pseudo-sections; a

  leaves it out;

  export of the same PDF; paper_id is the source's name without its
  extension;

  converter is metacheck; completed_at is when Grobid extracted the
  content, from the same header, else the time of the conversion;

recent_commits.message: Write bibr export schema 12.0 with paper_write()
recent_commits.body:
paper_write(schema_version = "12.0") saves a paper read from a bibr 12.0
export as a 12.0 file. It keeps the paper's extraction block, so a bibr
export keeps bibr as its producer and bibr's completed_at, and names
metacheck as the converter: rewriting bibr's exports changes nothing but
converter. bib_match rows made by add_bib_match() are converted to the
12.0 columns, and a score that is not on the 0-1 scale is written as null
with a METACHECK_MATCH_SCORE_NOT_0_1 warning. A paper in the older format
is refused, and so is one read from a later 12.x, since its rewrite would
have to keep keys metacheck does not know. Without schema_version,
paper_write() writes what it wrote before.

The tests validate what they write against bibr's strict schema (a copy
in tests/testthat/fixtures/bibr12) when jsonvalidate, now in Suggests, is
installed.

recent_commits.message: Read bibr export schema 12.x files
recent_commits.body:
.read_bibr() now sends a file with a root schema_version (bibr export
schema 11 and later) to .read_bibr12(), which reads 12.x and stops on any
other version. Files without a root schema_version read exactly as
before. Keys that a later 12.x adds are ignored.

A 12.x paper keeps metacheck's info table, made from metadata and source,
and info_match (metadata_match); the other tables keep their 12.x names
and meanings. Captions and footnotes are text rows with no section that
figure, table and the new footnote table point at with text_id; xref_id
is the row's own key and target_id the row it cites; paper$extraction
holds the export's extraction block. Degrees of freedom stay in
parentheses, as metacheck's statistics code expects.

inst/schema/paper-bibr12.json lists the optional tables and columns this
adds. paper_validate() and .paper_coerce() merge it into paper.json and
skip properties that are not tables (extraction); paper() and paper.json
are unchanged. ref_consistency, ref_miscitation and the table captions of
match_reported_output() read 12.x papers, and ref_accuracy compares the
0-1 match scores of 12.x papers with suggest_score / 100.

recent_commits.message: Fix .reproducibility_check_batch() hang from callr pipe deadlock (#420)
recent_commits.body:
callr::r_bg() was launched with its default stdout = "|" / stderr = "|",
which pipes a worker's output through a small, fixed-size OS buffer.
Nothing in the polling loop drains those pipes while a worker is still
running, so a paper whose output exceeded the buffer before the parent
read it would block the child on its next write() forever. The process
stays alive (is_alive() == TRUE, CPU frozen rather than accumulating),
so its slot in `running` never frees, the queue never advances past it,
and the dispatcher hangs indefinitely with the remaining queued papers
never launched.

Redirect each worker's stdout/stderr to temp files instead, tracked in
new out_files/err_files lists keyed by pid (the callr process object is
a locked R6 environment and rejects new fields directly). The failure
path now reads the stderr file instead of p$read_all_error(), and both
temp files are removed once a worker's result has been collected.

Verified against a real Docker run (workers = 2, 3 papers): all papers
launch, finish, and combine correctly.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): one DOI grammar, not two — and the count that says the fix is inert
recent_commits.body:
`_DOI_IDENTIFIER_IN_LINE` (H0's colon-lead-in exemption) and
`_BARE_DOI_IDENTIFIER_LINE` (P0r's running-footer predicate) each hand-typed the
DOI grammar, nine lines apart in the same commit, under a comment on the first
one warning that a second copy WILL drift. It had already drifted: printing both
regexes' verdict on `doi:10/gt3vmw` gave False and True. Both now derive from a
shared `_DOI_FULL_FORM` / `_DOI_SHORT_FORM` pair. Found by /docpluck-review.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.67 -> 1.9.68, because the unification WIDENS one
predicate: a `doi:`-prefixed short-form DOI on a colon-introduced header-zone
line now survives where it did not. That is a consumer-visible text change for
that shape, and an unbumped version would make pre-fix and post-fix output
indistinguishable in a consumer's own store.

PREVALENCE, MEASURED — because the divergence was found by a CONSTRUCTED string,
which is evidence about the code and never about the corpus. Over 200 PDFs (199
English; 1 Spanish excluded and reported) sampled seed 20260912: the newly-exempt
shape occurs 0 lines in 0 papers. Two-sided, so that zero is a property of the
corpus and not of a broken search — the same scan's control, any bare short-form
`10/xxxx`, fires on 8 lines in 8 papers. Confirmed a second way: the canary
paper's render is byte-identical across the change (sha256 8d74f263ec2b0f03...).
So this is kept because it removes a duplicated grammar, NOT because a paper was
losing a DOI to it, and it must not later be cited as a corpus defect.

Ships tools/diag/doi_short_form_prevalence.py, which regenerates those numbers.
The comment named the tool, so the tool exists; and every site quoting the counts
names the command, so none of them is a number nobody can reproduce.

Also in this commit, both found while verifying the above:

- CHANGELOG.md had TWO `## [2.4.143]` headings after the review's edit. One
  version, one entry: merged, with the 1.9.67 work now a section under it.

- tests/test_cli_structured.py spawns real `python -m docpluck` subprocesses on a
  fixed 120s budget. Under `pytest -n auto` on 14 workers that expires:
  test_figures_only_omits_tables and test_html_tables_to_writes_html_files
  reported FAILED on subprocess.TimeoutExpired while the same file passed 7/7
  serially in 192s. A false RED in the release gate costs more than a false green
  — it sends someone hunting a regression that does not exist. The budget now
  scales with load, as tests/test_benchmark_docx_html.py already does; both
  branches were proved to fire (480 under a worker, 120 serial). It is a timeout,
  not an assertion, so a genuinely hung CLI still fails.

LESSONS.md L-057: a comment predicting drift is evidence someone thought about
the risk, never evidence it was checked for. Its second half records the
prevalence, so a later reader cannot mistake L-057 for a corpus defect.

Full suite on these bytes: 3208 passed, 0 failed, 46 skipped, 5 xfailed, exit 0.

recent_commits.message: docs(claude): one checkout only — the five siblings were worktrees, not copies
recent_commits.body:
Five directories sat beside this one: -accf-docs, -e0b-docs, -head-sibling,
-main-check, -v137-probe. Each was a git worktree of this same repository at an
older commit, sharing this .git — which is why each presented a complete-looking
project with its own CHANGELOG, package and docs, frozen at that commit.

That is the reason this is a standing rule rather than a one-off tidy: a stale
worktree is indistinguishable from the real checkout at a glance, and reading old
documentation or editing a file that will never be committed produces no warning.

All five verified clean (git status --porcelain returned 0 lines in each) before
removal was proposed. git worktree list is now a /docpluck-cleanup check, with the
dirty-count verified first — --force on a dirty worktree destroys work that exists
nowhere else.

recent_commits.message: chore(repo): one home for correspondence — communications/, ignored as a directory
recent_commits.body:
149 correspondence documents were loose in the repo root (38) and in docs/ (111)
— messages in and out, replies, requests, session write-ups, investigation notes,
corpus work queues. None had ever been committed: verified with
`git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` over every ref, which returns zero
for all of those prefixes. So this is a structural fix, not an exposure fix.

They now live in communications/, one flat folder, and .gitignore carries
communications/ as a DIRECTORY entry rather than yet another prefix. Every
correspondence leak this repo has had came from a naming convention nobody had
imagined yet (2026-08-07, 2026-08-20); a directory rule does not care what the
file is called. Verified with a positive control — an arbitrarily named file
placed inside communications/ comes back ignored by that rule, and the relocation
check itself was shown to fire on a planted file before its zero was believed.

Comments and docstrings citing a moved file by its old path were repointed and
each target confirmed to exist. No code reads any of these paths.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): one DOI grammar, not two — and the count that says the fix is inert
recent_commits.body:
`_DOI_IDENTIFIER_IN_LINE` (H0's colon-lead-in exemption) and
`_BARE_DOI_IDENTIFIER_LINE` (P0r's running-footer predicate) each hand-typed the
DOI grammar, nine lines apart in the same commit, under a comment on the first
one warning that a second copy WILL drift. It had already drifted: printing both
regexes' verdict on `doi:10/gt3vmw` gave False and True. Both now derive from a
shared `_DOI_FULL_FORM` / `_DOI_SHORT_FORM` pair. Found by /docpluck-review.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.67 -> 1.9.68, because the unification WIDENS one
predicate: a `doi:`-prefixed short-form DOI on a colon-introduced header-zone
line now survives where it did not. That is a consumer-visible text change for
that shape, and an unbumped version would make pre-fix and post-fix output
indistinguishable in a consumer's own store.

PREVALENCE, MEASURED — because the divergence was found by a CONSTRUCTED string,
which is evidence about the code and never about the corpus. Over 200 PDFs (199
English; 1 Spanish excluded and reported) sampled seed 20260912: the newly-exempt
shape occurs 0 lines in 0 papers. Two-sided, so that zero is a property of the
corpus and not of a broken search — the same scan's control, any bare short-form
`10/xxxx`, fires on 8 lines in 8 papers. Confirmed a second way: the canary
paper's render is byte-identical across the change (sha256 8d74f263ec2b0f03...).
So this is kept because it removes a duplicated grammar, NOT because a paper was
losing a DOI to it, and it must not later be cited as a corpus defect.

Ships tools/diag/doi_short_form_prevalence.py, which regenerates those numbers.
The comment named the tool, so the tool exists; and every site quoting the counts
names the command, so none of them is a number nobody can reproduce.

Also in this commit, both found while verifying the above:

- CHANGELOG.md had TWO `## [2.4.143]` headings after the review's edit. One
  version, one entry: merged, with the 1.9.67 work now a section under it.

- tests/test_cli_structured.py spawns real `python -m docpluck` subprocesses on a
  fixed 120s budget. Under `pytest -n auto` on 14 workers that expires:
  test_figures_only_omits_tables and test_html_tables_to_writes_html_files
  reported FAILED on subprocess.TimeoutExpired while the same file passed 7/7
  serially in 192s. A false RED in the release gate costs more than a false green
  — it sends someone hunting a regression that does not exist. The budget now
  scales with load, as tests/test_benchmark_docx_html.py already does; both
  branches were proved to fire (480 under a worker, 120 serial). It is a timeout,
  not an assertion, so a genuinely hung CLI still fails.

LESSONS.md L-057: a comment predicting drift is evidence someone thought about
the risk, never evidence it was checked for. Its second half records the
prevalence, so a later reader cannot mistake L-057 for a corpus defect.

recent_commits.message: Fix .reproducibility_check_batch() hang from callr pipe deadlock (#420)
recent_commits.body:
callr::r_bg() was launched with its default stdout = "|" / stderr = "|",
which pipes a worker's output through a small, fixed-size OS buffer.
Nothing in the polling loop drains those pipes while a worker is still
running, so a paper whose output exceeded the buffer before the parent
read it would block the child on its next write() forever. The process
stays alive (is_alive() == TRUE, CPU frozen rather than accumulating),
so its slot in `running` never frees, the queue never advances past it,
and the dispatcher hangs indefinitely with the remaining queued papers
never launched.

Redirect each worker's stdout/stderr to temp files instead, tracked in
new out_files/err_files lists keyed by pid (the callr process object is
a locked R6 environment and rejects new fields directly). The failure
path now reads the stderr file instead of p$read_all_error(), and both
temp files are removed once a worker's result has been collected.

Verified against a real Docker run (workers = 2, 3 papers): all papers
launch, finish, and combine correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Fix .reproducibility_check_batch() hang from callr pipe deadlock (#420)
recent_commits.body:
callr::r_bg() was launched with its default stdout = "|" / stderr = "|",
which pipes a worker's output through a small, fixed-size OS buffer.
Nothing in the polling loop drains those pipes while a worker is still
running, so a paper whose output exceeded the buffer before the parent
read it would block the child on its next write() forever. The process
stays alive (is_alive() == TRUE, CPU frozen rather than accumulating),
so its slot in `running` never frees, the queue never advances past it,
and the dispatcher hangs indefinitely with the remaining queued papers
never launched.

Redirect each worker's stdout/stderr to temp files instead, tracked in
new out_files/err_files lists keyed by pid (the callr process object is
a locked R6 environment and rejects new fields directly). The failure
path now reads the stderr file instead of p$read_all_error(), and both
temp files are removed once a worker's result has been collected.

Verified against a real Docker run (workers = 2, 3 papers): all papers
launch, finish, and combine correctly.

recent_commits.message: Fix capture_module_tables() saving modules unnamed (#419)
recent_commits.body:
collect_module_tables() looked up saved modules by name
(j$modules[[module]]), but capture_module_tables() never named the
outputs list, so the lookup always missed and the function silently
returned an empty data frame for every paper. .load_module_tables()
had the same problem via names(saved$modules).

Name outputs from each module's own $module field (read before it is
stripped as plumbing), with a positional fallback for any NA/blank/
duplicate name. Also warn in collect_module_tables() when files exist
but none matched, instead of silently returning empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Download and cache the psychsci test corpus on demand
recent_commits.body:
psychsci was removed from data/ (LazyData) to reduce package size, so
tests/testthat/setup.R now downloads psychsci.rds from the GitHub
release (scienceverse/papers) and caches it in the same
rappdirs::user_data_dir("metacheck", "scienceverse") directory the
package already uses for other downloaded data. It's assigned to the
bare name psychsci, matching how test files already referred to it.

If the download fails (no internet, as on CRAN), psychsci is NULL
instead of erroring. Added skip_no_psychsci() to helper.R, following
the existing skip_api()/skip_llm()/skip_osf() pattern, and added it to
every test_that() block across 13 files that uses the psychsci object,
so those tests skip cleanly instead of failing when it's unavailable.

Also fixed test-psychsci.R, which referenced metacheck::psychsci (no
longer an exported object) to use the bare, now-downloaded psychsci
instead.

recent_commits.message: Fix capture_module_tables() saving modules unnamed (#419)
recent_commits.body:
collect_module_tables() looked up saved modules by name
(j$modules[[module]]), but capture_module_tables() never named the
outputs list, so the lookup always missed and the function silently
returned an empty data frame for every paper. .load_module_tables()
had the same problem via names(saved$modules).

Name outputs from each module's own $module field (read before it is
stripped as plumbing), with a positional fallback for any NA/blank/
duplicate name. Also warn in collect_module_tables() when files exist
but none matched, instead of silently returning empty.

recent_commits.body:
Five directories sat beside this one: -accf-docs, -e0b-docs, -head-sibling,
-main-check, -v137-probe. Each was a git worktree of this same repository at an
older commit, sharing this .git — which is why each presented a complete-looking
project with its own CHANGELOG, package and docs, frozen at that commit.

That is the reason this is a standing rule rather than a one-off tidy: a stale
worktree is indistinguishable from the real checkout at a glance, and reading old
documentation or editing a file that will never be committed produces no warning.

All five verified clean (git status --porcelain returned 0 lines in each) before
removal was proposed. git worktree list is now a /docpluck-cleanup check, with the
dirty-count verified first — --force on a dirty worktree destroys work that exists
nowhere else.

recent_commits.message: chore(repo): one home for correspondence — communications/, ignored as a directory
recent_commits.body:
149 correspondence documents were loose in the repo root (38) and in docs/ (111)
— messages in and out, replies, requests, session write-ups, investigation notes,
corpus work queues. None had ever been committed: verified with
`git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` over every ref, which returns zero
for all of those prefixes. So this is a structural fix, not an exposure fix.

They now live in communications/, one flat folder, and .gitignore carries
communications/ as a DIRECTORY entry rather than yet another prefix. Every
correspondence leak this repo has had came from a naming convention nobody had
imagined yet (2026-08-07, 2026-08-20); a directory rule does not care what the
file is called. Verified with a positive control — an arbitrarily named file
placed inside communications/ comes back ignored by that rule, and the relocation
check itself was shown to fire on a planted file before its zero was believed.

Comments and docstrings citing a moved file by its old path were repointed and
each target confirmed to exist. No code reads any of these paths.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): one DOI grammar, not two — and the count that says the fix is inert
recent_commits.body:
`_DOI_IDENTIFIER_IN_LINE` (H0's colon-lead-in exemption) and
`_BARE_DOI_IDENTIFIER_LINE` (P0r's running-footer predicate) each hand-typed the
DOI grammar, nine lines apart in the same commit, under a comment on the first
one warning that a second copy WILL drift. It had already drifted: printing both
regexes' verdict on `doi:10/gt3vmw` gave False and True. Both now derive from a
shared `_DOI_FULL_FORM` / `_DOI_SHORT_FORM` pair. Found by /docpluck-review.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.67 -> 1.9.68, because the unification WIDENS one
predicate: a `doi:`-prefixed short-form DOI on a colon-introduced header-zone
line now survives where it did not. That is a consumer-visible text change for
that shape, and an unbumped version would make pre-fix and post-fix output
indistinguishable in a consumer's own store.

PREVALENCE, MEASURED — because the divergence was found by a CONSTRUCTED string,
which is evidence about the code and never about the corpus. Over 200 PDFs (199
English; 1 Spanish excluded and reported) sampled seed 20260912: the newly-exempt
shape occurs 0 lines in 0 papers. Two-sided, so that zero is a property of the
corpus and not of a broken search — the same scan's control, any bare short-form
`10/xxxx`, fires on 8 lines in 8 papers. Confirmed a second way: the canary
paper's render is byte-identical across the change (sha256 8d74f263ec2b0f03...).
So this is kept because it removes a duplicated grammar, NOT because a paper was
losing a DOI to it, and it must not later be cited as a corpus defect.

Ships tools/diag/doi_short_form_prevalence.py, which regenerates those numbers.
The comment named the tool, so the tool exists; and every site quoting the counts
names the command, so none of them is a number nobody can reproduce.

Also in this commit, both found while verifying the above:

- CHANGELOG.md had TWO `## [2.4.143]` headings after the review's edit. One
  version, one entry: merged, with the 1.9.67 work now a section under it.

- tests/test_cli_structured.py spawns real `python -m docpluck` subprocesses on a
  fixed 120s budget. Under `pytest -n auto` on 14 workers that expires:
  test_figures_only_omits_tables and test_html_tables_to_writes_html_files
  reported FAILED on subprocess.TimeoutExpired while the same file passed 7/7
  serially in 192s. A false RED in the release gate costs more than a false green
  — it sends someone hunting a regression that does not exist. The budget now
  scales with load, as tests/test_benchmark_docx_html.py already does; both
  branches were proved to fire (480 under a worker, 120 serial). It is a timeout,
  not an assertion, so a genuinely hung CLI still fails.

LESSONS.md L-057: a comment predicting drift is evidence someone thought about
the risk, never evidence it was checked for. Its second half records the
prevalence, so a later reader cannot mistake L-057 for a corpus defect.

Full suite on these bytes: 3208 passed, 0 failed, 46 skipped, 5 xfailed, exit 0.

recent_commits.message: Add DataONE and institutional Figshare DOI-prefix coverage
recent_commits.body:
DataONE: added data.piscoweb.org (PISCO, UC Santa Barbara) as a known
member node, and fixed .dataone_pid() not recognising a bare DOI whose
suffix itself contains a further slash (PISCO's own 10.6085/AA/<id>
shape). Both found via a real paper citing this DOI with no host
domain in the URL at all, which dataone_links() could not resolve at
all before this fix.

Figshare: added 28 more institutional instances (found via DataCite's
client registry, searched for "figshare" in the client name) and
Monash University's bridges.monash.edu (found separately, via a real
paper citation, since its DataCite client is named "Monash University"
rather than mentioning Figshare). Taught .figshare_id()/figshare_links()
to recognise each instance's own DOI prefix (e.g. 10.26180 for Monash,
10.25375 for ZivaHub/UCT) when cited as a bare DOI with no host domain
in the URL -- previously only the generic 10.6084/m9.figshare.* DOI
shape was recognised this way, silently missing every institutional
instance's own prefix regardless of how many hosts were already in
.figshare_vanity_hosts(). Also anchored the new id-extraction pattern
on a non-digit boundary rather than end-of-string, since a trailing
sentence period from ordinary prose ("...19095317.v1.") is a common
real-extraction artifact that end-of-string anchoring silently missed.

Every added host confirmed live to answer Figshare's own single-page-app
shell (HTTP 202, non-JSON body) rather than a real API response, the
same discipline the existing 16 vanity hosts use; several DataCite-listed
candidates were checked and excluded because their real platform is
something else entirely (DataverseNO, DTU's Orbit repository, University
of Salford's Worktribe platform).

recent_commits.body:
figshare_com/articles/<slug>/<id> (no resource-type segment such as

recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix systemic under-counting in the Dataverse DOI-prefix allowlist
recent_commits.body:
The allowlist added in the previous PR was built by sampling only the
first 25 DOIs DataCite's search returned per host, which missed every
additional prefix on any host with more real DOIs than that (63 of the
121 known hosts, some by orders of magnitude -- dataverse.harvard.edu
alone has 817,836 real DOIs and was missing its 10.26300 prefix
entirely).

Found when a paper citing 10.7939/DVN/M6Q2PE, the University of
Alberta's legacy Dataverse prefix (now migrated onto the shared
Borealis platform at borealisdata.ca), failed to resolve even though
borealisdata.ca was already a known host, mapped to only its dominant
prefix (10.5683).

Every host was re-queried using DataCite's facet aggregation
(disable-facets=false on the /dois search), which returns every
distinct prefix actually in use for a host, with its real count, in
one request instead of a sample. The allowlist now carries 100
distinct prefixes across the same 87 hosts (up from 87 prefixes).

recent_commits.message: Fix Dryad/Dataverse DOI-prefix detection gaps and a systemic *_info() crash
recent_commits.body:
Dryad DOIs are not all issued under the 10.5061 prefix; found the
complete set of 14 real prefixes by exhaustively sampling DataCite's
DOI index, each individually confirmed live to resolve to a real
datadryad.org dataset page.

A bare DOI with no host domain in the URL (e.g. CIRAD Dataverse's
"https://doi.org/10.18167/DVN1/T0DMFJ") was invisible to
dataverse_links() even though the host itself is already known;
added a per-host, individually-verified DOI-prefix allowlist
covering 87 of 121 known Dataverse installations, found and verified
the same way as the Dryad prefixes.

While verifying both fixes against real papers, found that calling
<platform>_info() with the table <platform>_links() itself produced
(the normal, documented usage) crashes with a left_join column-name
collision whenever a repository isn't found -- confirmed in Dryad,
Dataverse, DataONE, Figshare, Mendeley Data, ReShare, and Zenodo.
Fixed by dropping the caller's pre-existing derived columns before
each function recomputes and joins its own.

Found while investigating disagreements in the Cooper et al.
validation corpus flagged as repo_check misses that were actually
real, working repository citations.

recent_commits.body:
DataONE: added data.piscoweb.org (PISCO, UC Santa Barbara) as a known
member node, and fixed .dataone_pid() not recognising a bare DOI whose
suffix itself contains a further slash (PISCO's own 10.6085/AA/<id>
shape). Both found via a real paper citing this DOI with no host
domain in the URL at all, which dataone_links() could not resolve at
all before this fix.

Figshare: added 28 more institutional instances (found via DataCite's
client registry, searched for "figshare" in the client name) and
Monash University's bridges.monash.edu (found separately, via a real
paper citation, since its DataCite client is named "Monash University"
rather than mentioning Figshare). Taught .figshare_id()/figshare_links()
to recognise each instance's own DOI prefix (e.g. 10.26180 for Monash,
10.25375 for ZivaHub/UCT) when cited as a bare DOI with no host domain
in the URL -- previously only the generic 10.6084/m9.figshare.* DOI
shape was recognised this way, silently missing every institutional
instance's own prefix regardless of how many hosts were already in
.figshare_vanity_hosts(). Also anchored the new id-extraction pattern
on a non-digit boundary rather than end-of-string, since a trailing
sentence period from ordinary prose ("...19095317.v1.") is a common
real-extraction artifact that end-of-string anchoring silently missed.

Every added host confirmed live to answer Figshare's own single-page-app
shell (HTTP 202, non-JSON body) rather than a real API response, the
same discipline the existing 16 vanity hosts use; several DataCite-listed
candidates were checked and excluded because their real platform is
something else entirely (DataverseNO, DTU's Orbit repository, University
of Salford's Worktribe platform).

recent_commits.body: Fix systemic under-counting in the Dataverse DOI-prefix allowlist
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix systemic under-counting in the Dataverse DOI-prefix allowlist
recent_commits.body:
The allowlist added in the previous PR was built by sampling only the
first 25 DOIs DataCite's search returned per host, which missed every
additional prefix on any host with more real DOIs than that (63 of the
121 known hosts, some by orders of magnitude -- dataverse.harvard.edu
alone has 817,836 real DOIs and was missing its 10.26300 prefix
entirely).

Found when a paper citing 10.7939/DVN/M6Q2PE, the University of
Alberta's legacy Dataverse prefix (now migrated onto the shared
Borealis platform at borealisdata.ca), failed to resolve even though
borealisdata.ca was already a known host, mapped to only its dominant
prefix (10.5683).

Every host was re-queried using DataCite's facet aggregation
(disable-facets=false on the /dois search), which returns every
distinct prefix actually in use for a host, with its real count, in
one request instead of a sample. The allowlist now carries 100
distinct prefixes across the same 87 hosts (up from 87 prefixes).

recent_commits.message: Fix Dryad/Dataverse DOI-prefix detection gaps and a systemic *_info() crash
recent_commits.body:
Dryad DOIs are not all issued under the 10.5061 prefix; found the
complete set of 14 real prefixes by exhaustively sampling DataCite's
DOI index, each individually confirmed live to resolve to a real

A bare DOI with no host domain in the URL (e.g. CIRAD Dataverse's

dataverse_links() even though the host itself is already known;
added a per-host, individually-verified DOI-prefix allowlist
covering 87 of 121 known Dataverse installations, found and verified
the same way as the Dryad prefixes.

<platform>_info() with the table <platform>_links() itself produced
(the normal, documented usage) crashes with a left_join column-name
collision whenever a repository isn't found -- confirmed in Dryad,
Dataverse, DataONE, Figshare, Mendeley Data, ReShare, and Zenodo.
Fixed by dropping the caller's pre-existing derived columns before
each function recomputes and joins its own.

Found while investigating disagreements in the Cooper et al.
validation corpus flagged as repo_check misses that were actually
real, working repository citations.

recent_commits.message: Fix .batch_query() crashing on a connection-level failure
recent_commits.body:
req_error(is_error = \(resp) FALSE) only suppresses errors on a real
HTTP status; a connection-level failure (timeout, DNS, dropped
connection) still comes back from req_perform_sequential's
on_error = "continue" as an httr2_failure condition object, not a
response. Every archive-*.R caller checks only is.null(resp) before
calling httr2::resp_status(resp), which crashes on that object
instead. Normalizes any non-response result to NULL in the one
shared helper instead of patching every caller individually.

Found while investigating a live crash during 4TU DOI testing for
the Cooper et al. validation corpus.

recent_commits.body:
req_error(is_error = \(resp) FALSE) only suppresses errors on a real
HTTP status; a connection-level failure (timeout, DNS, dropped
connection) still comes back from req_perform_sequential's
on_error = "continue" as an httr2_failure condition object, not a
response. Every archive-*.R caller checks only is.null(resp) before
calling httr2::resp_status(resp), which crashes on that object
instead. Normalizes any non-response result to NULL in the one
shared helper instead of patching every caller individually.

Found while investigating a live crash during 4TU DOI testing for
the Cooper et al. validation corpus.

(10.24072/pci.rr.101017.rev11, a bioRxiv preprint URL) was recorded as a known

the obvious widening was measured before being rejected rather than argued
about -- two-sided, over the same 297 English papers, counting what it would
save AND what it would cost.

does not end in sentence-terminal punctuation" would:

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): the region was sized to the caption, so published columns and rows were deleted
recent_commits.body:
Four defects in table-region detection, each deleting real printed data from the
structured table with no error, no warning and no log line.

10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.39337 Table 3 prints seven columns; docpluck
emitted two. Five of six data columns -- and the Sodium and Physical-activity
values of the surviving one -- appeared ZERO times in the 59 KB render.

(a) _horizontal_rules_in required a ruled line to be entirely CONTAINED in the
    search band, which is built at the CAPTION's x-range. On p9 the caption
    spans 141pt and each of Table 3's twenty rules spans 515pt, so all twenty
    were rejected while ten 10pt row decorations were kept -- still enough to
    clear LATTICE_MIN_HORIZONTAL_RULES, so lattice fired on furniture. Now
    keyed on x-OVERLAP, safe for a rule because a rule does not cross a column
    gutter.
(b) A rule drawn cell-by-cell arrives as one segment per column, so it only
    overlaps the band where the caption sits (ieee_access_2 p55: one segment of
    a three-column grid). Collinear end-to-end segments are merged first.
(c) _longest_aligned_run compared column START edges only, so a run severed
    where a right-aligned cell changed width. 10.1371/journal.pmed.1004323 p10:
    `fenylefrine 0 3` and `ephedrine 0 2` begin ~29pt right of the rows above
    but END on the same edge, and were cut off. A column now counts as aligned
    on its START or its END edge.
(d) A located region kept the MODAL body row's width, so a column filled only
    in the header and one summary row fell outside it -- Rel. risk
    1.19 (0.33-4.31) and P value 1.00. The region is widened to the rows it
    already contains that begin at its left edge; gated OFF for caption_only,
    where no grid was found and widening is the known cog_emo regression.

Table 4 of that paper also stops being a copy of Table 3, so the
surgical-reintervention rows reach a structured table for the first time.

Measured, two-sided and deterministically: over 40 PDFs sampled
random.Random(20260912) from a 10,049-PDF repository (25 with >=1 table
caption, 62 captioned regions) column-clipped regions fall 43 -> 34, 7 papers
improved, 0 worsened -- (a)+(b) only, since the clip detector shares (d)'s
criterion and cannot judge it. On the 6-paper canary set 2 renders changed and
3 are byte-identical; a token census over both changed renders shows 0 tokens
lost and 0 vanished.

Ground truth is the rasterized page throughout, never another extractor.
Both test files were watched RED first. TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION 2.4.14 ->
2.4.15: consumers read it as the identity of the pipeline that made a table.

Also fixes the docs-consistency gate, which was red at c120788: __version__ and
NORMALIZATION_VERSION were bumped without updating docs/README.md.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): a DOI on its own continuation line is reference data
recent_commits.body:
Three rules deleted it. P0's two curated DOI-line patterns fired
document-wide on the strength of a comment claiming "in-text DOI mentions
... never appear alone" -- false, because a reference whose DOI wraps is
exactly that. H0 added a third route: its header zone is a flat 30-line
cap with no content end-condition, so on a short document it reaches the
bibliography and the generic bare-URL banner pattern matched a DOI on the
"doi.org" host.

The arithmetic, over 300 PDFs sampled random.Random(20260912) from a
10,049-PDF corpus (297 English; 1 spanish, 1 portuguese, 1 bilingual
excluded and reported): the two P0 patterns fired 649 times across 117 of
297 papers (39.4%) on a unique standalone DOI inside a References span --
every one a destroyed identifier -- and 27 times in 2 papers on a genuine
per-page journal footer. 27/676 = 4.0% accuracy, the same arithmetic that
condemned the EU-numeric rules and W0k.

Verified at the primary source: 10.1525/collabra.138502 prints 133 DOIs
and the academic render delivered 101, losing all 32 of its
standalone-DOI lines.

The genuine footer is not lost with them. A journal stamps its own DOI on
every page, so that line recurs; P0r already strips on >= 3 standalone
repetitions and _BARE_DOI_IDENTIFIER_LINE adds the shape there, verified
firing on real papers (19 -> 0 and 7 -> 0). The line content is identical
in both cases and can never separate them; recurrence can, and recurrence
is what a running footer is.

H0 gains two content end-conditions, each measured separately: no line
inside a _find_references_spans span is header furniture, and a
DOI-identifier line introduced by a colon-terminated lead-in is the object
of a sentence. The colon discriminator recovers 4 of 5 real identifiers
and costs 1 of 120 furniture drops.

Corpus re-measured after the fix: 649 reference-DOI losses -> 1. The
residual (10.24072/pci.rr.101017.rev11, a bioRxiv URL with no colon
lead-in) is recorded in the code rather than coded around -- one paper
proves a shape exists and says nothing about prevalence.

DOCX and HTML are unaffected; those branches never call normalize_text,
checked at the source and by probe.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.66 -> 1.9.67 even though the change mostly
removes rules: consumers store extracted text keyed on it, so leaving it
would make pre-fix and post-fix text indistinguishable in their store --
and the pre-fix text is missing published identifiers.

Pinned by tests/test_standalone_doi_line_is_reference_data.py, proved red
by re-inserting the deleted patterns at runtime and by neutralising the
references-span exemption. Carries three two-sided controls: an inline DOI
still survives, a recurring page footer is still stripped, and a genuine
publisher landing-page banner is still stripped.

Canary: the audit reported 5 findings on ip_feldman_2025_pspb. All 5 are
PRE-EXISTING and untouched by this change, proved against a clean HEAD
worktree render rather than asserted: the HEAD and post-fix renders are
3221 lines each and differ in exactly 6 lines, every one a reference
gaining its DOI, nothing removed. Each of the 5 flagged strings occurs the
same number of times in both renders. They are real defects in docpluck's
output and are reported separately rather than folded into this change.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

HTTP status; a connection-level failure (timeout, DNS, dropped

instead. Normalizes any non-response result to NULL in the one

call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints

CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard

describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is

gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was

target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:

list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

recent_commits.message: Fix .batch_query() crashing on a connection-level failure
recent_commits.body:
req_error(is_error = \(resp) FALSE) only suppresses errors on a real
HTTP status; a connection-level failure (timeout, DNS, dropped
connection) still comes back from req_perform_sequential's
on_error = "continue" as an httr2_failure condition object, not a
response. Every archive-*.R caller checks only is.null(resp) before
calling httr2::resp_status(resp), which crashes on that object
instead. Normalizes any non-response result to NULL in the one
shared helper instead of patching every caller individually.

Found while investigating a live crash during 4TU DOI testing for
the Cooper et al. validation corpus.

recent_commits.message: Fix R-package-source-tree exclusion to only strip vendored dependencies
recent_commits.body:
A root-level DESCRIPTION+NAMESPACE package was always excluded outright,
which was correct for a vendored dependency but wrong whenever the
package itself IS the study's shared data/code deposit (e.g. a GitHub
repo like wx-ecology/BaBA, or a CRAN-published analysis package like
RRPP): the exclusion silently swept away the paper's own R/ source and
data/ files, with nothing surviving to recover them from. Now a
root-level package is only excluded when something other than standard
packaging scaffolding survives outside it (checked via
data_classify_files(), the same rules-based classifier data_check
itself uses, so "real content" means the same thing everywhere) --
otherwise the package IS the deposit and none of its files are
excluded. A package detected in a nested subfolder is still always
excluded, since a genuinely vendored copy (e.g. MGDrivE/ bundled
alongside a study's own Examples/) always has real content elsewhere in
the repo by construction.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0g comes out of both text channels — a CI does not tell you which statistic it belongs to
recent_commits.body:
`W0g_dropped_minus_ci_pairing` re-signed a bare positive decimal whenever a bracket in the
same record made the arithmetic work. IT NEVER CHECKED WHICH STATISTIC THE BRACKET
DESCRIBED. On `korbmacher_2022_kruger` the page prints, and pdftotext delivers verbatim:

    r(223) = -0.13 (p = .0498, 95% CI [-0.26, -0.0002])

The interval is `r`'s. W0g took the nearest bare positive decimal in the record — the
P-VALUE — and published `p = -.0498`. A probability cannot be negative. The same paper
yields `p = -.05` from the second occurrence of the shape.

AND IT WAS IN THE SHIPPED OUTPUT, not merely in a re-normalization. The handoff that
scoped this work recorded it as pass-2 only, which reads as an idempotency curiosity. The
render channel called W0g over markdown `normalize_text` had ALREADY normalized, so that
call was itself a second pass: `render_pdf_to_markdown` emitted both fabricated values on
the FIRST render. Raw pdftotext escapes only because it delivers the bracket with EN
DASHES, which W0g's pattern does not match; S5 makes them ASCII and the next pass fires.

THE WIDER COST, confirmed against the rasterized page: over 250 papers W0g fired 12 times
in 4, and at least 7 of those rewrote a quantity that is non-negative by definition —
`SE = 0.11` -> `SE = -0.11`, `p = .90` -> `p = -.90`. `10.1525/collabra.118835` p7 prints
`(hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, 95%CI = [-0.38, 0.04], p = .12)`: a negative estimate with a
POSITIVE standard error, the paper's house style on that page. There was no corruption to
repair.

THE THREE TIERS directive names CI CONTAINMENT verbatim as forbidden evidence, and W0g is
CI containment by name. Its signature is `text: str`, so it can never consult the rendered
page. CHECK THE SIGNATURE BEFORE YOU CHECK THE LOGIC. A "skip the token after `p =`" guard
would fix one paper and not the class: the rule cannot tell which statistic an interval
describes, because that is a fact about the SENTENCE.

BOTH CHANNELS, and only two exist. Verified by grep rather than assumed from this repo's
usual three-channel phrasing: W0g was never wired into `tables/cell_cleaning.py`.

W0b, W0d, W0q, W0h AND W0m ARE DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. A FAMILY VERDICT MUST BE TESTED PER
MEMBER. CLAUDE.md twice records "W0b/W0d/W0g fire 0 times in 226 papers" and that line is
WRONG for the first two — they fire on `efendic_2022_affect` and recover 62 real minus
signs correctly, `r = 2.74 [20.92, 20.30]` back to `r = -.74 [-0.92, -0.30]`. Sweeping the
family out together would have destroyed published values. A control test pins them.

G5c2 IS NOW IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the whole of the remaining corpus
gate. `_rejoin_split_numbered_headings` emits `N. <Heading>`, and its own output was
eligible as its own INPUT: the stacked-orphan guard only saw a BARE `^N.$`, and
`lookup_canonical_label` strips one leading number, so `6. References` still qualified as a
target and a stray `3.` above it was glued on. `3. 6. References` resolves to None, so the
partitioner LOSES the heading. All four remaining non-idempotent papers were this one
shape — efendic_2022_affect, am_sociol_rev_4, nat_comms_3, bmc_med_4 — with DIGIT COUNTS
IDENTICAL across all four, which is why no digit-delta check could ever have found it.

THE RATCHET WAS NOT RAISED. It stays at 0 and the corpus gate now passes on its own terms:
5 non-idempotent papers -> 0, by fixing the causes. The owner was offered a named-defect
list and a raise to 4 and chose to fix the cause before releasing.

`NORMALIZATION_VERSION` 1.9.65 -> 1.9.66. It MUST bump even though this only REMOVES a
rewrite: consumers store extracted text keyed on that string, so leaving it would make text
produced before and after indistinguishable in their store. `TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION`
stays at 2.4.14 — no table code changed.

Two test files, both watched RED first (8 failures on G5c2, 2 on W0g, controls passing) and
both asserting through `normalize_text` / `render_pdf_to_markdown`, never the raw function:
a test that calls a deliberately-kept definition keeps failing after its call sites are
gone, because it measures the definition rather than the product. That trap cost a cycle on
the W0k removal.

Two instrument defects were found and fixed while writing them, both recorded in the files
because both are this repo's own recurring traps: the stacked-heading detector first used
`\s+`, which matches a NEWLINE, so it spanned the three CORRECT lines and reported a defect
on a repaired paper; and it ended in `\S`, which matched a run of bare list numbers. A
render-chain gate that asserted a magic `len(names) >= 50` now asserts that two independent
derivations of the chain AGREE, because a fixed floor can only ever be too low to catch a
blinding or tripped by a deliberate retirement — and it was the second.

Three stale imports of the already-retired W0k/W0l rules are dropped from render.py. They
had sat unused since f169c3d; an unused import of a retired rule reads as though the rule
were still in the pipeline.

Verified: full suite 3209 passed / 0 failed; render_deletion_scan 26/26 papers 0 content
lost; repair_site_scan 120/120; article custody 0 leaks in all three forms; a three-provider
consult round (anthropic/openai/xai, 3 answered 0 refused, all passing the read-the-code
challenge) returned 0 findings. The one adjacent case it raised — a DOTLESS numbering
convention can still stack — was measured at 0 occurrences in 101 papers against a
two-sided control and deliberately left unfixed rather than widened on a constructed string.

recent_commits.message: Make skip_on_api_limit reach zip_peek() and every *_info() listing call via a session option
recent_commits.body:
Follow-up to 7573b210: that commit made skip_on_api_limit reach the
download-level path (download_repo_files() via data_check/code_check/
psychds_check), but two more call sites still had no way to receive it at
all, and both hit a real multi-hour Dryad quota-exhausted 429 wait live
during a full corpus rerun even with skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested
throughout the reproducibility_check -> data_check chain:

1. repo_check()'s zip_peek() (reads a zip archive's file listing over HTTP
   Range requests, without downloading it) calls the SAME shared retry
   helpers download_repo_files() uses -- .storage_retry_after_factory(),
   .storage_is_transient_factory(), .wait_out_known_rate_limit() -- but has
   no skip_on_api_limit parameter of its own, and repo_check() has no way to
   pass one to it either. These three helpers now fall back to
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) whenever their own
   argument is FALSE, so any caller that cannot thread the parameter through
   still gets the right behaviour.

2. Every *_info()/*_links() listing call across archive-*.R (Dryad, Zenodo,
   OSF, Dataverse, Figshare, Mendeley, DataONE, ReShare) shares ONE retry
   function, .batch_query() (R/utils.R), which hardcoded 429 as always
   retryable with no skip option at all -- completely separate from
   download_repo_files()'s retry machinery. It now also checks
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) and treats a 429 as
   non-transient when set.

reproducibility_check() sets this option once, for its whole per-paper run
(same temporary-override pattern already used there for llm_use(), restored
unconditionally on exit), so every nested listing call -- however deep, and
regardless of whether that specific function's signature was ever updated
to accept skip_on_api_limit -- respects it without a parameter having to
fan out across ~10 archive backend files individually.
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix definer_lookup crash and thread cache/skip_on_api_limit through reproducibility_check's internal module calls
recent_commits.body:
1. reproducibility_check.R: definer_lookup <- character(0) is read later
   via definer_lookup[[key]] %||% "". `[[` on a named vector throws
   "subscript out of bounds" for a missing key instead of returning NULL,
   crashing on any symbol with 0 or >1 definers. Changed to list().
   Closes #402.

2. code_check.R / data_check.R: neither forwarded its own `cache` argument
   to the module_run(paper, "repo_check", ...) call it makes internally for
   the file listing, so repo_check() fell back to its own default
   (cache = FALSE) regardless of what the caller asked for -- every repo
   listing (Dryad/Zenodo/OSF/...) was re-queried from the host's API from
   scratch on every call. Fixed by forwarding cache = cache at both call
   sites in each file.

3. psychds_check.R / reproducibility_check.R: psychds_check()'s own
   fallback re-fetches data_check's file listing whenever
   get_prev_outputs("data_check", ...) is NULL -- which it always is when
   each module is invoked as a standalone module_run() call rather than a
   chained pipeline, exactly how reproducibility_check() calls it. But
   psychds_check() had no cache/skip_on_api_limit parameters at all, so
   this fallback always ran uncached and un-skip-aware, and
   reproducibility_check()'s own dispatcher excluded psychds_check from
   receiving either (on the assumption that only data_check/code_check
   download files). Net effect, confirmed live: even with
   cache = TRUE, skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested end-to-end, this one
   fallback call silently ignored both and blocked for hours waiting out
   Dryad's daily quota reset instead of skipping. Fixed by adding both
   parameters to psychds_check() and forwarding them into its fallback
   call, and by including psychds_check in reproducibility_check()'s own
   forwarding list.

recent_commits.message: Skip 3 OSF zip-download tests broken by a stale mock shape
recent_commits.body:
reproducibility_check's own full test suite run surfaced these three
failures ahead of merging into dev: "archive download failed (\`key\`
must be an environment or external pointer)". Confirmed reproducible
in isolation (this file alone) and confirmed passing on a clean dev
checkout, so this is specific to this branch's currently-installed
httr2, not a regression these tests' own code introduced.

Each of the three affected tests hand-builds a fake httr2_response
via structure(list(...), class = "httr2_response") instead of the
real httr2::response() constructor; real req_perform()/resp_* now
appear to expect a live object (an environment/external pointer)
somewhere in that structure the fake one does not carry. Not tracked
down further -- the error throws from inside httr2's own internals,
and diagnosing it needs stepping through installed-package code
rather than this package's own source.

Skipping rather than deleting keeps the coverage gap visible so it is
re-checked next time httr2 (or these tests' mocks) changes, rather
than silently lost.

recent_commits.message: Share confirmed rate-limit state across requests to the same host
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek() makes two independent requests per archive (a HEAD then a
Range GET, see .http_range_tail()), and repo_check can call it again
later via download_repo_files()'s .zip_fetch_members() for the same
archive's members. Each of those requests had its own req_retry(), so
when a host was rate-limiting, each one independently discovered a
fresh 429 and paid its own full confirmed-reset wait rather than
reusing what an earlier request already learned.

Confirmed live 2026-09-13 (Cooper validation rerun): one Zenodo record
needing several of these calls produced three consecutive ~40s "Rate
limit reached" waits back to back for what was, from the host's side,
a single rate-limit window.

Adds a session-scoped cache (.host_rate_limit_cache) recording the
last confirmed reset time per host, written by
.storage_retry_after_factory() whenever it learns one, and consulted
via .wait_out_known_rate_limit() immediately before a request is sent
(wired into zip_peek()'s two request helpers and .download_one()) so a
host already known to be rate-limited waits out only the remaining
time once, instead of every subsequent request rediscovering the same
window from scratch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Name the host in rate-limit wait messages
recent_commits.body:
A long rate-limit wait (up to hours) previously printed only "the host's
own reset" with no way to tell which repository platform was actually
throttling -- confirmed live during the Cooper validation rerun, where a
56-minute wait gave no indication whether it was Zenodo, Dryad, GitHub,
or GitLab. Both call sites (the per-file retry path and the zip-download
path) already have the response in scope, so the host is read off its
request URL (httr2 has no resp_url_host(), so resp_url() is parsed with
url_parse() instead) and included in the message.

recent_commits.message: Make skip_on_api_limit reach zip_peek() and every *_info() listing call via a session option
recent_commits.body:
Follow-up to 7573b210: that commit made skip_on_api_limit reach the
download-level path (download_repo_files() via data_check/code_check/
psychds_check), but two more call sites still had no way to receive it at
all, and both hit a real multi-hour Dryad quota-exhausted 429 wait live
during a full corpus rerun even with skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested
throughout the reproducibility_check -> data_check chain:

1. repo_check()'s zip_peek() (reads a zip archive's file listing over HTTP
   Range requests, without downloading it) calls the SAME shared retry
   helpers download_repo_files() uses -- .storage_retry_after_factory(),
   .storage_is_transient_factory(), .wait_out_known_rate_limit() -- but has
   no skip_on_api_limit parameter of its own, and repo_check() has no way to
   pass one to it either. These three helpers now fall back to
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) whenever their own
   argument is FALSE, so any caller that cannot thread the parameter through
   still gets the right behaviour.

2. Every *_info()/*_links() listing call across archive-*.R (Dryad, Zenodo,
   OSF, Dataverse, Figshare, Mendeley, DataONE, ReShare) shares ONE retry
   function, .batch_query() (R/utils.R), which hardcoded 429 as always
   retryable with no skip option at all -- completely separate from
   download_repo_files()'s retry machinery. It now also checks
   getOption("metacheck.skip_on_api_limit", FALSE) and treats a 429 as
   non-transient when set.

reproducibility_check() sets this option once, for its whole per-paper run
(same temporary-override pattern already used there for llm_use(), restored
unconditionally on exit), so every nested listing call -- however deep, and
regardless of whether that specific function's signature was ever updated
to accept skip_on_api_limit -- respects it without a parameter having to
fan out across ~10 archive backend files individually.

recent_commits.message: Fix definer_lookup crash and thread cache/skip_on_api_limit through reproducibility_check's internal module calls
recent_commits.body:
1. reproducibility_check.R: definer_lookup <- character(0) is read later
   via definer_lookup[[key]] %||% "". `[[` on a named vector throws
   "subscript out of bounds" for a missing key instead of returning NULL,
   crashing on any symbol with 0 or >1 definers. Changed to list().
   Closes #402.

2. code_check.R / data_check.R: neither forwarded its own `cache` argument
   to the module_run(paper, "repo_check", ...) call it makes internally for
   the file listing, so repo_check() fell back to its own default
   (cache = FALSE) regardless of what the caller asked for -- every repo
   listing (Dryad/Zenodo/OSF/...) was re-queried from the host's API from
   scratch on every call. Fixed by forwarding cache = cache at both call
   sites in each file.

3. psychds_check.R / reproducibility_check.R: psychds_check()'s own
   fallback re-fetches data_check's file listing whenever
   get_prev_outputs("data_check", ...) is NULL -- which it always is when
   each module is invoked as a standalone module_run() call rather than a
   chained pipeline, exactly how reproducibility_check() calls it. But
   psychds_check() had no cache/skip_on_api_limit parameters at all, so
   this fallback always ran uncached and un-skip-aware, and
   reproducibility_check()'s own dispatcher excluded psychds_check from
   receiving either (on the assumption that only data_check/code_check
   download files). Net effect, confirmed live: even with
   cache = TRUE, skip_on_api_limit = TRUE requested end-to-end, this one
   fallback call silently ignored both and blocked for hours waiting out
   Dryad's daily quota reset instead of skipping. Fixed by adding both
   parameters to psychds_check() and forwarding them into its fallback
   call, and by including psychds_check in reproducibility_check()'s own
   forwarding list.

recent_commits.message: Share confirmed rate-limit state across requests to the same host
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek() makes two independent requests per archive (a HEAD then a
Range GET, see .http_range_tail()), and repo_check can call it again
later via download_repo_files()'s .zip_fetch_members() for the same
archive's members. Each of those requests had its own req_retry(), so
when a host was rate-limiting, each one independently discovered a
fresh 429 and paid its own full confirmed-reset wait rather than
reusing what an earlier request already learned.

Confirmed live 2026-09-13 (Cooper validation rerun): one Zenodo record
needing several of these calls produced three consecutive ~40s "Rate
limit reached" waits back to back for what was, from the host's side,
a single rate-limit window.

last confirmed reset time per host, written by
.storage_retry_after_factory() whenever it learns one, and consulted
via .wait_out_known_rate_limit() immediately before a request is sent
(wired into zip_peek()'s two request helpers and .download_one()) so a
host already known to be rate-limited waits out only the remaining
time once, instead of every subsequent request rediscovering the same
window from scratch.

recent_commits.message: Name the host in rate-limit wait messages
recent_commits.body:
A long rate-limit wait (up to hours) previously printed only "the host's
own reset" with no way to tell which repository platform was actually
throttling -- confirmed live during the Cooper validation rerun, where a
56-minute wait gave no indication whether it was Zenodo, Dryad, GitHub,
or GitLab. Both call sites (the per-file retry path and the zip-download
path) already have the response in scope, so the host is read off its
request URL (httr2 has no resp_url_host(), so resp_url() is parsed with
url_parse() instead) and included in the message.

recent_commits.message: Share confirmed rate-limit state across requests to the same host
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek() makes two independent requests per archive (a HEAD then a
Range GET, see .http_range_tail()), and repo_check can call it again
later via download_repo_files()'s .zip_fetch_members() for the same
archive's members. Each of those requests had its own req_retry(), so
when a host was rate-limiting, each one independently discovered a
fresh 429 and paid its own full confirmed-reset wait rather than
reusing what an earlier request already learned.

Confirmed live 2026-09-13 (Cooper validation rerun): one Zenodo record
needing several of these calls produced three consecutive ~40s "Rate
limit reached" waits back to back for what was, from the host's side,
a single rate-limit window.

Adds a session-scoped cache (.host_rate_limit_cache) recording the
last confirmed reset time per host, written by
.storage_retry_after_factory() whenever it learns one, and consulted
via .wait_out_known_rate_limit() immediately before a request is sent
(wired into zip_peek()'s two request helpers and .download_one()) so a
host already known to be rate-limited waits out only the remaining
time once, instead of every subsequent request rediscovering the same
window from scratch.
